I picked up this game due to my recieving a coupon which made this already cheap package nearly free. I had some issues with this game, and despite it's infuriating second to last level, overall I would weigh up this as a positive experience more than a negative one. This game's premise is you are a clone boy with a hoverboard, and with help from you seemingly kindly Grandpa, you must stop a mysterious robot invasion. This platforming title has one primary objective each level; collect all the coins, then get to the portal exit. This is executed fairly well throughout the game, but there are some occasions of downright frustration.
The relatively simple yet solid gameplay here is only slightly undermined by the at first irritating controls, which become much more managable as you progress, or at least they did for me. Using 'A', and 'D' or the Arrow Keys to move, 'W' or the up arrow to jump, and holding the SPACE Bar to hover is slightly challenging at first, especially if like me you are used to SPACE being Jump more often. In early gameplay this will probably get you killed a bit, but this event will decrease and hopefully decease as you keep playing. What is irritating however is when your Jump + Hover, which is by far the highest propulsion possible without a Grav Lift, is too short to reach a platform or area, by miniscule amounts.
By far the most frustrating and beneficial factors come with Deaths however. Upon being killed, you are instantly back to the beginning of the level. No checkpoints, no in level saves, ever. As hard as this sounds, which it can be, especially in f
ing Level 19, you respawn with absolutely no penalty whatsoever. No coins lost. However it could be seen as a penalty that enemies respawn, which they do. Now to be fair, without this the game may be too easy, however it is annoying.
Speaking of enemies, there are sentient ones including standard Robots, which fly and damage you if you touch them, Robots with inbuilt firearms,
!!!, invincible robots on a track, and a boss at the end of the game. Also against you are non sentient enemies, like Electricity barriers, and.. well I actually can't think of any others. I have no problem with any standard enemies, EXCEPT the Robot with a gun. NERF THAT T
T!! Not only does it aim at you with a 360 degree rotating gun, but it can have pixel perfect accuracy, and worst of all wait for the perfect moment to shoot. Trust me, it may sound like fun difficulty, but you will rage at these. Aside from that the Boss is the only other one I want to discuss, however SPOILER WARNING. Reading my section on the Boss will ruin the twist in the game which while predictable, is still one of the cooler parts of the game. As such, I shall do the Final Words first, then do a spoiler warning and talk about the boss.
WORTH THE PRICE: YES
FINAL VERDICT: 6/10 - Good Game, worth picking up as it is worth the price, however could be improved in areas.
>>SPOILER ALERT<<
So if you are here now then you have either seen the Boss in game or just don't care about the spoiler. Fair enough. The boss is actually the Grandpa, who, in a twist that I myself prefectly predicted, turns out to be evil, and the one who presumably built the robots in the first place. The boss is fun and well made for the level, however to the Devs of the game, PLEASE MAKE IT SO HE CAN'T SPAWN KILL YOU. Several times when he killed me he teleported to my spawn. Most of the time this is fine as he is atop blocks and you can simply dodge him and get out. However in one incident, this was NOT THE CASE. His main attack, swinging his arms with electricity as hands, was timed just PERFECTLY, and he was in the PERFECT POSITION, so that EVERY TIME I spawned, he instantly killed me. This happened 3 TIMES. Please fix this. Aside from that he is fun, and works well with the level as you have to run along him to get the coins you need before he dies, dropping the last few so you can exit, and win the game. Thanks for reading if you got this far, hope this helped.

Before I say anything about this game YES its a "walking sim" YES all you do is walk around, open a bunch of drawers and chests, yes yes yes. If you are one of the "why play a game when all you do is walk around" "how is this even a video game" type of people then apply that logic to any other video game. If all you do is play CS:GO a game where "all you do is shoot people" with no actual story, why are you trying to downplay a game such as this? This game is beautiful in its own creepy twisted way..
NOW for the game, right off the bat let me just say you CAN blow through this♥♥♥♥♥♥in like an hour and a half. However going through the game in an hour and half would just prove that you did nothing aside from bare min and probably watched a guide here and their when things got "hard". I am usually not the type to buy into horror games jam packed with jump scares, but Layers of Fear does these scares so well. Every scare is perfect, they fit the game very nice that NONE of these scares feel cheesy. The atmosphere of this game is phenomenal. Playing this game using Hyper X Cloud II headset and I must say the audio quality of this game is great, never did I hear parts of the game where audio sounded bad. The "music" you hear through out the game is great, much like everything else in the game it fits PERFECTLY! The only draw back that I think this game has is operating cabinets and drawers so frequently. I have not 100% this game but I do plan on it, and to do this youre going to have to open a ♥♥♥♥♥on of cabinets and dressers etc. The issue is that when cabinet drawers are so close together sometimes its tedious to try and open the right one. I often times find myself trying to get my hand icon (the icon that indicates opening something) on the right thing but my mouse just doesnt want to open it. Its tedious at times but its nothing super major or game breaking.
This game is centered around understanding ones self and art. The relation is very interesting and you learn slowly as your progress through the story what everything means and what is going on. Almost as soon as you start the game,♥♥♥♥♥♥gets weird and to me thats amazing. The art style of this game is incredible, all the paintings are mesmerizing. Often times I found myself just gazing at hallways filled with paintings. Speaking of hallways, there is alot.. alot of them feel the
..  actually almost all of the areas you go to feel the same and thats because they are..
. The devs have done an AMAZING job of playing tricks on your mind, entering multiples of the same room yet there is just a subtle difference. The subtlety might be so miniscule that some people might completely over see them. Others with a keen eye on detail will catch them almost every time. I often found myself saying "wasnt that painting just over their..." "wait where did the ______ go?" "wasnt I just here".
TL;DR - Amazing ♥♥♥♥ing game, dont rush through and actually pay attention to story and every penny you spent will be well worth it.

This is a brilliant masterpiece of a game, though somewhat marred by strokes of cliched mediocrity.
Pro:  Brilliant concept.  I love how the theme of painting carries throughout the game, both in the classic paintings throughout the house, and in how paintings and paint are used to create mood and tell the story.  The game is exploration towards finishing a painting.  Consistency in the theme (art and painting) is a major positive for this game.
Con:  This is a very minor criticism, but I think that, considering how much classic art is in the public domain, I'd like to have seen the repetitions of paintings used more judiciously:  by which I want to say that repetition of the same painting in various rooms should have a meaning.  Sometimes it does, but sometimes it feels somewhat random, like the creators were just filling space, and considering how important art is to the theme of the game, I felt that this random feeling to the placement of paintings detracted.
Pro:  Light and shadow and texture are used beautifully throughout the game.  The movement of light and shadow, the movement of colors, the blurring and distortion of paintings and rooms:  all these things were used with amazing creativity and balance in the game.
Con:  Again, minor gripe, but the sound was sometimes used for a cheap jump scare.  Instead of relying on serious anticipation and intellectual horror, sometimes they used unevenly loud (sometimes obnoxiously loud) sounds to jar us.  While this CAN be a good thing, I felt, for the most part, the use of sound was not up to the same standard of the rest of the game.
Pro:  I felt that the story was intelligently presented.  The authors used very minor touches to give an almost impressionistic presentation of the story, rather than handholding us and hitting us over the head with the script.  What we get is a hazy, vague scene that has a stronger emotional impact than if they'd just had someone tell us exactly what happened.
Con:  Visually, there were cliche elements, such as the stuttering, distorted witch-figure haunting the house.  And there seem to be a lot of little touches that are cliche, and it's a shame because in such an original game, these cliches really do stand out more than they ordinarily would in a much more mundane game.
Pro:  The use of rooms for disorientation was very well-done.  As well, I appreciated how important information was hidden in drawers and cabinets here and there.
Con:  For a game that relies on the use of doors in its theme, it's a shame that the actual mechanic for opening and closing doors is not more smooth.  I'd much rather simply click on a door to open it, rather than trying to wiggle the mouse around to figure out which way it should go.  As well, although I liked searching for clues, I felt that there weren't enough things to see to justify the enormous number of drawers and cabinets.  Having a FEW more things to look at would have been nice.
Overall, while I feel I got my money's worth from the game, I finished the game in about 4 hours.  There IS some replay value in going back to try to figure out things i missed (for example, I never figured out the clue to the ouija board, and went to the next room to look for clues ... and the door locked behind me.  Couldn't go back and solve the puzzle.
Still, overall, I'd recommend the game, especially when it's on sale.

I really don't get it. I got this game from a bundle, and lucky me that I did.
I have finished this game in 110 minutes according to Steam. It has 5 trading cards to drop, of which I got 4 - which means I have to just idle this game just to get all cards, the game's length isn't long enough. It gives achievements for pretty much every little step you make in progression.
The game finished way too fast and the solutions were pretty obvious and straight-forward (up until one point where you had to fumble and guess with inventory, but that's with all point & clicks on a certain point in game, so not holding this specifically against this one). How can a point and click that got finished in under 2 hours be priced normally for € 5.99?

I could pretty much, after leaving the apartment, predict what was going to happen. And that doesn't make a fun point & click game, a type of game that - in my opinion - should focus on story & exploration.
I have the two other episodes as well in my list, but I won't be playing them. There hardly was something introduced here, there's nothing pulling me to that second episode. Maybe I'm missing out some achievements for 'not leaving it on my backlog' (yes, this episode actually has an achievement to reward you for not keeping it on your backlog), but I wouldn't want it either.
If short, obvious and straightforward point & clicks are your thing, go ahead (in perhaps a bundle somewhere), but don't buy it for full price. It's simply not worth it

One of the most mediocre games I've ever played. Nothing works well -- not the boring combat, not the derivative futuristic setting, not the unceasing boss fights, nothing nada zip. The AI is brick-wall stupid, and team members will only follow the most basic commands until they lose complete focus and decide to take cover or launch straight into the enemy instead. The audio commands don't work properly, and getting the game to recognize what you're trying to say is nearly impossible without a high-end microphone. The Trust System adds absolutely nothing to the overall story arch besides making it harder to boss the AI team members around. Gamepad controls don't map properly. The setting is filled with nothing but constant grey-on-grey environments, and the characters are the kinds of shallow stereotypes that are so particular to Japanese games. Even worse, Binary Domain suffers from that horrible console affliction known as QTE-itis -- quicktime events and cut scenes dominate a exasperatingly large part of the game, and real playable action is rare.
I'm boggled as to why such a mediocre game gets such good user reviews. It's as if people here have never played anything other than Gears of War or Azura's Wrath or other games of that ilk. Variety is the spice of life, folks, and the beauty about playing on an actual computer is that you have literally dozens of genres to choose from. Skip Binary Domain and play something better.

This game honestly caught me by surprise. I thought it was just gonna be another run of the mill cover based shooter with little to nothing to offer pretty much anyone. As someone who pretty much hates games based entirely around the concept of coverbased shooting, I can very much recomend this game.
It's a pretty solid game too, having some pretty decent length to it, and an interesting idea about your crew mates. At the begenning of each section you have the choice of two supporting characters out of the lot. As you play with each character they slowly start to trust you better, following orders and responding to praise better. This doesn't really pan out much in gameplay though, it has practically no effect other than the two or three lines you'll hear them spout consantly. It really made me get into the characters and story though, I got transfixed by a lot of the stuff that happens in this game that I just can't spoil.
Other than that, the game can get away with huge spectacular bossfights because of the setting it has, and most of those are very cool and very enjoyable. Once you get past the rediculous lack of effort that went into the PC port for this game(middle mouse to reload? Seriously?), we have a slightly janky but very enjoyable game about shooting robots in neo-Tokyo.

This review will be in comparison to its predecessor, Banished.
Upgrades and raids are the only two major additions.
Upgrades: produces universal improvements to most processes.
Disasters: raids send several enemies that attack the village and must be killed either by building defensive buildings or by taking control of a citizen to manually kill the raiders. I believe the developers have plans for a flood scenario which seems very interesting.
Crops: seeds are now gained through expeditions instead of trade which previously incentived commercialization.
There is no clarity on the difference between different vegetables and fruit.
Bakeries offer alternative processed food options for well being but note that they aren't immediately influenced by upgrades very well and are hardly worth it.
Crop variety requires a much greater foundation.
Gathering huts are now worthless making low density spread out villages very much more difficult and not worth while.
From this, options are consolidated for the player.
Trade: processed materials can be more quickly acquired but cultivation remains the greatest source of profit. Charcoal takes so much time to make that lower quality tools are given purpose early on; never make a kiln, just a merchant and donkey distributor.
Trades happen as often as the player desires without wait, giving them incredible viability.
From this, intermediary items have more worth, of course they still become worthless later in the game.
Castle: gives a direction to the player but is not needed. The player can defend manually for as long as they need to before towers don't cost a thing.
Illness: if the player isn't prepared, they may suffer tremendously. Herbs no longer increase general wellness.
The changes are enough to give a good reason to revisit what is essentially Banished, but I don't think its better. For city building it does have some nice additions but requires serious performance improvements.

Graphics

Music
Hotline Miami two keeps most of the same artist from the previous game with the new ones being a welcome addition. The game presents amazing track after track with almost none missing a beat

While not particularly scary beyond the odd jump scare, Layers of Fear is a truly superb piece of Gothic Horror. Playing it, one is instantly reminded not only of "The Portrait of Dorian Grey" - Oscar Wilde's classic Faustian pastiche is directly referenced at the beginning of the game - but also Edgar Alan Poe's "The Oval Portrait", which is a firm personal favourite of mine.
The Poe influence is indeed unmistakable throughout , especially given the overall angle that as a player you increasingly come to realise you are in fact the monster of the piece in spite of the bizarre supernatural entities that dog the game's anti-hero at every turn as he struggles through the cavernous internal labyrinth of his own tortured psyche. Couple this will almost photo-realistic visuals which bleed and ooze into maddening surrealism over time and we have what could easily be one of the best atmospheric pieces of recent time.
The only real flaw with Layers of Fear is that it feels shorter than it should be. While the game itself is flawless, it is possible to complete Layers of Fear in about four hours and as such the first play-through ends a little too quickly.
Thankfully, this does nothing to detract from the overall product. Ultimately, this is a game designed to outline the struggles of the artistic process by expanding on many of the less glamourous aspects of the creative industries; addiction, obsession; isolation and altered states of reality. Those who like blood and gore should probably stay clear but if you like meaning behind the terror then this is definitely for you.

The producers of this game, are clearly big fans of the P.T. demo, the main monster even looks the same. They are desperately trying to copy the atmosphere from the Kojima masterpiece, that never came to be, but for the most part, they fall way short and instead rely on jump scares.
It's a shame because the graphics are very nice and so are the audio, they also pull some amazing trippy warping of reality, that are genuinely very well done and I honestly did save quite a few screenshots. But graphics wont save you, if the story is lacklustre and scares are poor and too far in between. Furthermore the way that the route through the house is established, it completely destroys the sense of discovery and instead feels like a on-rails ride, that you are unable to divert too far from. The game is also kinda short, only lasting 3-4 hours to completion.

First, something about myself to frame this: I don't care much for superheroes, I watch the Hollywood movies if/when I fancy, and that's all; some I like, some I think are just junk. And I don't watch much TV besides the news.
The game then: the superhero theme stays accessible, never got any impression I was missing anything, but that was not the case for pop culture references, which will make much of this game feel dated and inaccessible in not too long a while, I'm afraid.
That said, I thought the writing never quite kicked into gear, the humor overlabored and falling flat on its face, until the final stretch of this episode, after you've passed all of your audition tests, and those would be 4. The voice acting also felt kind of dull, never lending any extra weight or liveliness to the lines, but this may as well be a direction issue, rather than a problem with the performers themselves, a few of whom you may be recognizing.
From the mechanical and execution point of view, loading screens pop up every time you walk into a different room, not just separate locations, also there is no way to make the PC warp to an exit, something that is expected of an adventure games, having it been the case for decades. This means downtime, when you are either staring at the PC crawl toward an exit or waiting for the loading screen to finally disappear: taken individually, they're not that much of an annoyance, but it all adds up, and the lack of snappiness makes trying different things and solutions more of a chore than it needs to be.
When a game is not very good for most of the playtime, we should just say that's the way things are, so this is going to be a thumbs down. On the other hand, the twist and ending are making me hopeful that other episodes will finally find their stride: Kyle has stopped being the prototypical unlikable, ne'er do well, dunce in favor of a more original and interesting character, and "Nurse Kevorkian" shows comedic potential. Now if only they had found a way to make Mel the Brit less of a drag...

I really like my point-n-click adventures. The main thing I like about them is story and puzzles, and it's a bonus when it has actual character, too. This game has none of these things.
It looks pretty... I think this is another result of animation/modelling students/professionals thinking that game development is about animation/modelling, rather than gameplay and story-telling. No, being an artist or technical artist does not make you a game developer.
I thought it looked like it might be fun. It isn't. It is unimaginative, unwitty, and labourious.
If it wasn't for the obnoxious, monotonous dialogues and the terrible attempts at humour, this game might be kinda playable, but the bad jokes and dragging dialogues make this game more of a painful chore than entertainment. I've so far spent several hours struggling to keep my eyes open.
The puzzles don't make a whole lot of sense, either. Basically, wait until one of the characters in the game tell you exactly what you need to do. That is the single puzzle solving mechanic that is employed: let the game solve the puzzles for you. Any attempt at logic is not going to get you too far.
Also, it's short, and you're duped into paying several times to get the full game.
If you laugh at the mention of fart, sex, or anything attempting to be obscene but coming across as simply puerile, then you might enjoy this. If you're into masochism, then you'll want to pay full-price for this one. Otherwise, I'd suggest you avoid it all together.

So as this is my first review ever, I thought the privilege should go to Life is Feudal: Forest Village.
TL:DR This game, though it can be trying at times, it is a wonderful world to explore and make your own. Is it worth the price tag, most definitely, specially if you get it on sale.
Onto the reveiw!
At first, I have to say, I was skepical about this game given the mixed reveiws. I watched some videos on it and instantly fell in love.
It reminded me of the city builders I love to play, the added bonus was when I saw someone go into first person mode and literally step into that world. They walked around their creation, and played around with the first-person controls. I was completely floored. It was such a wonderful idea. I loved it so much I bought the game the next day.
There is so much to do in this game, from making a small village just getting by, to a huge thriving kingdom. I'm sure at least an hour or two of my time was used just tilling farms so I could get it harvested on time.
The planning in this game is crucial, like, where should I put my healers shop, did I put my bakery close enough to a barn, do I have enough food for winter. This game can be complex sometimes, but 90% of the time its relaxing and alluring.
It's truely another world you can immerse yourself into and make your own.
Now don't get me wrong, there are a few things that need some re-balancing or touched up in the game but overall it doesn't take away from the overall feel of the game. You're going to spend hours planning out your first village, making sure everyone has enough food for winter, and playing around in the first-person mode, marveling at your own creation that, to be honest the price tag is well worth it.
I honestly can't wait to see what they do with it next!
I look forward to the next update.

Binary Domain is one of those games that starts off terribly, but somehow manages to bring itself back round to awesome. I knew this game started life as a basic port for the PC, but after playing through the entire game, I can see that some things were patched. :P
Okay, so first up, the story starts off pretty cliche and dumb, following Dan (player's character) and Bo sneaking into another country. The dialogue was awful at times, especially when they start "chatting up" the girl in Charlie's team. The cringe factor was so high here! However, after the first half hour or so, the pace picks up and so do the cut scenes. At first, I wasn't sure how to react to the amount of cut-scenes there were, but, the animation and story allows you to sit back and enjoy it. And In all honesty, I could see this being an animated film, it felt that good at times.
Of course, it's not all good. This game still has some strange port issues like the main screen showing "?," which seems to do nothing! Navigating menus with a mouse provides no cursor, instead simply moving between options, left-right-up etc. etc. Also, I initially started playing this game with an Xbox 360 pad and noticed that the game was not showing me Xbox pad buttons for the actions on-screen. Instead, it shows keyboard keys! Bizarre. It gets better... If you want to change around any buttons, you're out of luck as, the options menu doesn't have a redifine keys function. Although, I did find out that it should be editable via the config files. So, I guess that's not too bad.
That's the worst of it, though. Get over these points and you'll find a solid 3rd person cover shooter. And the game played flawlessly with no glitches, too. So, hats off to it for that! Another nice feature was being able to choose who to go into combat with, i.e. choose Bo and Faye, while the other half of the team take a different route. Or make an all-male team leaving the girls to go in another direction. Definitely nice to see some real choices that somewhat affects your playthrough. It certainly makes me wonder if the game's story plays out any differently due to a players' choices.
Yet another nice feature is when your AI friendlies sometimes offer to take the lead on something, leaving you to do something else. Even asking which threat you want to deal with, the boss or the troops in another direction. Awesome! And the story, dagnamit, that was pretty good. As I said, I could sit and watch this game as an animated cg film. There's still some corny dialogue, but it's still popcorn worthy :P
Overall, it's a ton of fun if you like 3rd person cover shooters. And I didn't even cover the range of weapons, upgrades, voice-recognition directions to AI characters, etc. etc. There's a lot to check out in this game and I'm damned pleased that I picked this up. It's not amazingly long, but still, there's a lot of bang per buck on this one. Thumbs up!

So after meeting quite a few a people who for lack of a better word appear to be brainless,here is a simple way to win 3 objective battles quickly: if the enemy is rushing to defend the middle objective,send a 3 man squad to capture the one closer to the enemy base.They should of course bypass the middle objective by taking a longer route where they will find a lightly defended or completely defenseless objective.I personally single-handedly captured at least 3 objectives this way,which forced the enemy to divert their attention and let my team capture the other objectives.Charging constantly an objective defended by 7 or 8 enemies will just be a waste of time.
In my experience the community is quite nice,some involuntary friendly fire is sometimes a pain,but other then one or two people killing team mates voluntarily there were no issues.When paired with a good team though the game is excellent,I lost track of how many times we turned defeats into wins.On the other hand it's also true you sometimes get a team of new people on one team and veterans on the other,which makes it a bit unbalanced,but hey this is WAR,if you want a balanced game all the time this might not be your game.
If you really want to do great in this game,there's two ways to achieve it:
1) Take the easy way around and invest a good amount of money to have the best equipment
2) Be ready to grind your way up to that equipment,which gives it a sense of realism when you consider that such equipment would have been handed out to the troops who showed potential.
The real snag I have so far is that there are just 3 objectives on each map,which although it makes for short matches with plenty of action,it becomes too repetitive after a while.The inclusion of just 1 more objective would in my opinion make for completely different tactical choices: Do you just capture and hold 2 objectives,sending scouts to harass the enemy,or do you try to capture all of them risking to be stretched too thin?
This and maybe the inclusion of a couple more vehicles,maybe even new Nations,would very much spice up this already great game in my opinion.Personally I'd like riding in a Panther taking out enemy vehicles as it's always been my favourite tank but I feel every nation would benefit with a couple more vehicles.Or how about possibly adding Japan and adding maps based for example around Guam,Saipan and other hotspots of the Pacific War?
In the end this is a free game,and sure it has micro-transactions but noone is forcing you to pay up,if you wanna take the easy way out that's your choice.Personally I might show my support by buying a couple extra soldiers or a Sturmgewehr when I unlock it,but it's a CHOICE, NOT an OBLIGATION.
Recommended.
9.5/10
P.S. Encountered an issue which was solved in less than 48 hours, Customer Support is excellent,deserves extra points just for that.

I have played quite a bit of this game. About 200 hours with steam and the stand-alone launcher combiner.  While I was intially drawn to the game and actually enjoyed it a fair bit, I just cannot recommend this game.
The problems:
-The development has been a crawl.  I have been playing for close to two years and while there have some good updates, they don't seem like they will ever be finishing this game.
-Content is lacking here.  With few updates comes few maps and content.  You will consistently be fighting on the same maps, and if there is a new map, it will have the same assets.
-Balance has gotten worse with every update.  They introduced the "balaced battles" where generals do not influence the game; however, not even these matches seem to be able to correctly match sides evenly.  Get used to being spawn camped by tanks.
-Free-to-Play.  This game seemed to have a good model earlier in its development, but it is now becoming very hard for a player that is spending no money to compete.  The great classes, guns, and vehicles require a ridiculous amount of time to earn and repair. The amount of gold that items and ribbons require is just ludicrous.
In the end, you have a game that is already passing its peak, and will never be finished.  I wanted this game to be able to satisfy my WWII craving until the next AAA WWII shooter came around, but it's just not going to make it.

I've been following Russpuppy for a while. Spooky Cats was good for a laugh and offered up and affordable (if a little bare bones) platformer and The Deletion was a very fun and challenging minimalist platformer in the tradition of geometric games like Thomas Was Alone.
Hover 2030 admittedly has a strange aesthetic--a pixel character straight out of the Atari age and yet smooth, clean environments. The sprite is nice but the levels all basically look the same. While not much to look at, Hover 2030 is actually quite fun and very challenging. If you weren't given unlimited lives in this game it would be difficult beyond belief.
The basic goal of each level is to collect all the coins to open up the exit. You must use your hoverboard to perform high jumps and float your way toward out-of-reach coins. Along the way you'll encounter a host of irritating enemies (especially time sensitive electric gates). Controlling the hoverboard takes a bit of time to get used to and once you have it mastered the levels get progressively harder. The game tops it all off with an end boss which must be defeated in a very clever way.
Also, be on the look out for the Russpuppy himself (the blue dog in the logo)  in a cameo in a much appreciated celebratory bonus level at the end of the game.
Hover 2030 is not a perfect game--the audio fx are a little grating and the gameplay can be a bit frustrating at times--but it's a solid effort with some addictive moments and an interesting hover mechanic. You can't go wrong with the price. I look forward to more games from this developer.

Supreme League of Patriots is a point and click adventure game, developed by No Bull Intentions, releasing in January 2015. The game has huge comical elements with the focus more on the story and plot rather than the game play.
Other than moving around and interacting with objects in the game world, there isn't really much to do. The puzzles are easily worked out and are very few and far between. The majority of the few puzzles revolve around combining the objects you have picked up, the only remotely challenging puzzles I had was the controls and UI, which I will go more onto later in the review.  All of the NPCs in the game can be interacted with and have plenty of dialog options for you to exhaust.
Graphically, Supreme League of Patriots looks colourful and childlike, with most of the character looking more like they have been pulled out of a Nickelodeon. Whilst some people may not think that is a bad thing, but since the game is actually supposed to be based around comic book super heroes, I would have liked to have seen a more comic book theme going on. On top of the mediocre graphics, the animation is not really much better either, some of it either just looks awkward or just plain awful. Characters make really odd movements to get around objects, their walk animations looks janky and odd.
From what I have played so far, the story is following a stereotypical American young man, and boy to the play on the stereotypes, and a witty sarcastic English man. The two together make quite a funny pairing, and the dialogue between all of the characters are really good too. Each piece of dialog has some sort of comical attachment to it as well, it will have you chuckling along through it all. The first chapter ends at a good moment and sets up the second part nicely. You can pretty much guess some of the plot points before they even, they are just that obvious, but it will still be interesting to see where they take it.
Every character in the game is voice acted to an extremely high standard, the English character is spot on with the accent. There are some voices which are quite obviously taking the mick out of some well-known celebrities such as Simon Cowell and David Hasselhoff.
Since there isn't that much game play involved at least in the first chapter of the game, there is hardly any difficulty involved so far. Like I said, the only difficult part I had was the actual user interface, there is no form of tutorial to explain how to interact with objects you have picked up, you'll also need to combine items together in good Point and click fashion - this involves you opening one of the many inventory screens you have access to. When scrolling towards the bottom of the screen, one of the inventory screen pops up, this is where you select the item which is "active" in the game world that lets you "use" items with items in the world. This took me a good few minutes to figure out on my own - this could of easily of been solved with a small tutorial explaining it.
The first episode took me two hours to complete, this I feel is an OK length since there is another two episodes to come, which I would anticipate to be of the same length if not more.  I did actually find myself wanting to get a couple of the achievements as well, leading to me saving at key points so I could reload to unlock the achievements.
The technical side of the game is sound. I played the game using the Steam Controller using a very basic control configuration and had no problems. Obviously the game will work just as well with the mouse though. An odd issue I did run into is that the game will not run in windows mode on certain resolutions, it will just crash to desktop giving you a message saying it’s not supported - not a massive deal, but still something which should not be a problem.
To sum up, so far, Supreme League of Patriots looks to be an interesting title. I am looking forward to see where the game takes the plot, and I am hoping to see a little more puzzle and game play elements being added into the later stages of the next few chapters. I am more looking forward to seeing more of the comical back and forth between the two characters. People who really enjoy the British sense of humour will really get a lot of enjoyment out of it; if you don't enjoy it, you'll probably be better of skipping this title because it is basically a walking joke the whole way through.

Now, the thing the game really gets good is the sort of humor they have, i really enjoy the ironic referencial type of humor the game offers, the dev said he aimed at humor used in popular shows like South Park, Family Guy and The Simpsons as he enjoyed that type of humor himself.

The third error with the game which i really don't get, is why it was split into 3 games. Layers of Fear is a terrific horror game that delves into the dark depths of an insane artist's mind. A man who goes from being a famous painter with a good life, beautiful wife, and an innocent daughter to a madman obsessed with finishing a particular painting with the most grotesque tools possible. He'll delve deep into his own hopes, dreams, fears, regrets, and nightmares to get what he wants.
Here is a summary of the Pros (+) and Cons (-) of this game:
+ Beautiful and performance friendly visuals. Environments are packed to the utmost brim with details, without requiring insane hardware to run it at reasonable settings. The aesthetic oozes ambience and atmosphere.
+ In depth narrative that is easy to understand... if you're willing to look for the clues and read up. A deep story about a painter's life progressively going to hell.
+ Simple and rewarding interaction. It reminds me of Amnesia, where you use mouse movements to push or pull open doors and other things.
+ A solid amount of subtle scares brimming with tension and fear. Some jumpscares are actually decent for once.
+ Excellent audio and music! Creepy ambient music really sets the mood.
- Some scares are too heavy handed and last longer than they should, and very few are unintentionally hilarious. There is a reliance on jumpscares in this game. If you don't like them, then do not get this game.
- The game is almost a walking simulator, if not for a few puzzles that do rely on some thought. This is a bad thing to me, but can be a good thing for a few others.
- The DLC expansion pack, Inheritance, is more of a surreal narrative experience rather than horror most of the time. The viewpoint gimmick gets old very quickly. (Fisheye effect, to simulate the character being very small.)
- Limited gameplay options besides interacting with objects and looking at things.
The Game is great and creepy :-)

Man, with as good of a concept as Wartile is, it kills me that I’m apparently as bad as I am. It could be the game itself, but I am willing to take partial fault here. However, given some of the map set ups in how they will walk you into single-fire arrow canyons, it’s possibly not all me. The difficulty is a bit much for me and does seriously detract from the fun I could have had. Would I like a local multiplayer option? Yes I would. Would I also like to not have to unlock multiplayer? Yes I would. Maybe the rest of the development cycle will change how the game works more in my favor, maybe not. As Wartile stands currently, I couldn’t easily recommend it even though it seems many others are doing just fine and enjoying themselves.
Full Impressions:
Digitized board games have been a thing for a while now. I remember playing Monopoly on my NES and enjoying it a ton more because it wasn’t a super long, drawn-out, boring test in frustration. (That’s not bitterness talking; I had a bad experience.) This concept has been around for a while and has done well. In comes Wartile, which, as far as I know, wasn’t based on an actual board game and tries some new concepts that I haven’t played around with before. Real-time turn-based (RTTB from now on because jeez) gameplay… is that even a thing? Well it is now. Wartile looks and works well for what it is, but is it fun? Let me break it down for you.
First up, I want to commend the developers of Wartile for the aesthetics of the game because if Wartile is anything, it’s beautiful. The game pieces look fantastic as do the boards that you play them on. The way the combat looks can be a little clunky looking, but it’s figurines stuck on little circle stands trying to poke each other so that’s no big surprise. This is one of the things that drew me to the game in the first place. It’s kind of like people who will gawk over finely painted 40k figures, but had no intention to play.
The RTTB gameplay is a neat spin on how the tactics games play. Your characters are always attacking as long as they are in range and have line of sight. You can’t attack through a friend because friends aren’t meat shields! There is a circle on the bottom of your piece that lets you know when you can move them again. This will let you reposition to get the height advantage or to start attacking from behind which seems to do more damage. The enemies have the same abilities though so make sure you hamper them as best you can. If you’ve got a shield bash ability, that keeps them in place for a while (even though it seems like they can still attack which I think is goofy). A person with a pole-arm can do the same thing although without a shield obviously and from a distance. (I use this move to run a good chunk of the time or keep a sword wielder at bay, but mostly to run.) While I’m talking about the abilities, using them can also be frustrating because the cards representing them have a hit-box to click on. When you mouse over them and it makes them larger, but that doesn’t mean you can click on all of the enlarged card, and you still seem to need to click where they originally were. That got frustrating when I was trying to time a much-needed heal.
While the gameplay is cool and it looks great, Wartile is hard as crap for me. I’ve played and beat numerous tactical games, but for some reason I cannot defeat the third level here. It’s very frustrating. I’ve gotten pretty far into it, but my forces are all eventually killed. There is an “energy” system in place for your abilities and you get more by completing certain tasks. If you run out, you can’t use moves like heal or heal… which I have twice in my hand because reasons. Some bad guys will block almost every attack even with three men on them from the front and back and shield-bashed to boot. This isn’t even a boss character. Then you’ve got those freak’n archers that don’t stop plinking my hind quarters when I’m stuck in a 1-tile wide path with a baddie blocking it.
I’ve gone back to get more gear and that didn’t seem to help too much. It did make me feel better, but didn’t even the odds. I was able to go back and finish previous levels at a harder difficulty setting which, as I said, gave me more gear. Not better gear, just more variety. I wasn’t looking for Thunderfury here, but that would have been nice. Not all my men made it out, but with more gear options I had hope at least. Hope that was extinguished thereafter.
I was kind of leery about trying out the multiplayer because of how bad I was doing, but I haven’t unlocked it. Yes, you have to unlock it. At my going rate this isn’t going to happen. Of course, given how well I’m playing right now, I’m not sure I would be very good against other people who have unlocked this mode. I’d probably want to pull more hair out. I think I’ll keep my sanity (or at least I’ll fain like I have the option to opt out even though I can’t get in).

The Evil Within is truly an UNDERRATED game IMHO. Its not GOTY material but its fun enough for me to go back and play it a second time.

The Evil Within is outstanding, and is easily as good as Resident Evil 4. That being said, you'll get pretty frustrated if you try to play it like Resident Evil 4. "Running and gunning" isn't viable in The Evil Within. Sometimes it's better to run, and traps trump direct combat the vast majority of the time. For example, you're better off getting everyone in the room stuck on an electric bolt and dispatching them with a match than you are trying to shoot everybody.
The game caters well to a variety of playstyles. My first run through was 12 hours (I was lost most of the time, and looking for collectibles), and my most recent was 3 hours. Akumu difficulty is immensely rewarding, and there's a great deal of satisfaction to be had when you're breezing through the dangerous encounters spread throughout.
I do have a complaint, and it's regarding those slow walking sections that seem to plague modern games. When possible, there are ways to speed it up:
Method (1) Aim your weapon. Walking while aiming is significantly faster than dealing with the default 'slow walk' speed.
Method (2) In the event that you can't aim your weapon (or don't have one), melee attack repeatedly. The repeated lunging motion is also quicker than the 'slow walk' speed.
Method (3) Tap the fire button (R1/RB for gamepads). This lets Sebastian run through liquids he'd have to wade through normally, for some reason.
I'd score this a 9/10. It's my favorite 2014 game (although the best one was Shovel Knight imo). I'd strongly recommend playing it. I'm looking forward to the sequel.
For reference, I got all of the base game achievements in about 40 hours.

tl;dr: It's like L4D in a lot of ways, but it also has some unique and interesting concepts. Maybe wait for it to go on Sale though.
I haven't played a lot of this but for right now, so far so good. To get the obvious out of the way, yes this is basically Left 4 Dead. It's got similar gameplay, similar special enemies, similar etc. For most people this would be a turn off and I guess I wouldn't blame them, why pay $30 for this game when L4D2 is like $20. This is just my opinion, but L4D2 is starting to look a bit worn out. There's only so much mods can do to keep a game relevant and honestly the only reason I go back to L4D2 is to try out the most ridiculous mods on the workshop. When that bit of hype is dead I just uninstall the game and forget about it. Vermintide is something (kinda) new and it keeps me interested in the game for a few different reasons.
One thing I really enjoy about the game is its environments. I don't know much about the Warhammer series and all the lore and things like that, but playing the game makes me want to look some of this stuff up. The environments in this game look really cool and it reminds me of what the first L4D had going on; desolate and somewhat bleak looking towns and forests that add a sense of dread and a bit of terror to the game, unlike in L4D2 where it was nice and colorful. Now this could be a bad thing depending on your preferences, some of you might enjoy a colorful world, but for the mood that Vermintide is trying to go for, I think the bleakness is fitting.
Another thing I liked about the game is the interactions between the characters. I always like to when characters have personalities instead of just being a silent emotionless weirdo, especially if its a game like this where you're more than likely playing with other people. Like in Killing Floor 2. You have these really interesting characters, all with different backgrounds and unique personalities, but they don't really talk to each other unless it's something like "I'm reloading". It kinda sucks cause like... I really want to know what the German WWII soldier has to say to the hip, young, Dutch DJ. L4D did this kinda well, but the characters would mainly talk to each other in like scripted events. In Vermintide, they pretty much talk all the time, whether they are complimenting each other, insulting each other, talking about each other's history and background, etc. Again, this may be a bad thing depending on preference, I know some people enjoy a bit of silence, but I thought it was nice to see these characters come alive.
Speaking of which, I should mention the game utilizes a class system. Instead of each character being pretty much the same, they are seperated into classes. There are 5 classes/characters to choose from, each with their own loadout and ablilities. There's the Soldier, Pyromancer, Wayfinder (Archer), Witch Hunter, and.... Dwarf class. There is also a Leveling system, as in you can level up. I'm not sure if each class has its own level, or if the level is just universal and i'm pretty sure there isn't any stat building so. You do unlock somethings in the game, like access to things in the little hub world and sometimes you get weapons and items.
The game has an interesting (although sometimes unfair) loot system. Unlike L4D, you can't just pick up a weapon you find on the ground, you earn new weapons for your characters by completing missions. When you complete a mission, you will have the chance to earn loot in a dice game. You roll several dice (i think like 7) and hope that the dice land on a special symbol. More symbols = Better Loot (I think). You can  also earn special dice that have better loot payouts by collecting hidden Tomes and.. these other things that I only know as grims. It adds a bit of challenge because the tomes will take up your healing item slot and the grims will actually make it so you have less health capacity if you choose to take them (i think the grims do more than this actually, but i'm not sure).
I've heard some people complain that this game is unoptimized, saying the usual crap like "Oh man i've got like ♥♥♥♥ing 4 GTX 970s and a Titan with 6400 GBs of RAM and i still can't get this game to run on the worst settings". I really have no clue what they're talking about, I am using a kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gaming laptop Lenovo Y510p, I've got the graphics pretty much set to max, except for a couple things, and the game runs fine, I don't get 60 fps, but it still runs smooth enough. It's not like this game is unplayable..
There are some where glitches however, I heard a teammate complain that he randomly died out of no where (But honestly i think he just fell of a ledge and didn't notice maybe?). The game isn't super stable but... i mean... its better than Fallout 4 at least in terms of stablility.
Gameplay wise, it's fun. I can't say how fun it is if your just playing by yourself, but with people it's a lot of fun. One thing I noticed is that it's kinda hard. I always thought L4D2 was pretty easy, even on Expert at some points. I mean, if you play a campaign with smart people, the game is pretty easy. But this game got pretty challenging even on the Normal difficulity (There are 5 difficulites, Normal is the second easiest). Now this may be because i'm still new to the game, but Idk, I was playing with the some high level players and we would still get our asses kicked sometimes. So if you're into difficult games, this aspect may be a plus.
If you enjoy melee combat and fantasy world type stuff similar to The Elder Scrolls or D&D, than I would recommend getting this game. Maybe not at the full $30, maybe wait for a sale or Humble Bundle, but yeah you should get it.
Worth every dollar i paid for this. And i paid two dollars.

tldr: Its a melee version of l4d2 with warhammer setting but not as polished, no custom maps, only survival besides coop, weapons of different quality that have different stats depending on rarity, double spawn on specials of the same type in the same area (which is not balanced), somewhat iffy optimization, only player hosted games and really unbalanced map for the same loot.
Pros
Modern graphics
Different equipment builds you can use (so long as you get the loot drop)
Daily missions keep people somewhat playing the same maps
Different classes and unique playstyle
Good amount of lore(background story)
Awesome banter amongst the group
Storyline
Forge system
The lore with this game is pretty intriguing it keeps things interesting for a lot longer than you would think. The banter in the group gives you good laughs from time to time they decide to talk. Missions keep people doing the same maps which alternate everyday. The forge system allows you to manage your weapons recycle ones you dont use and use the materials to make other weapons (rng what weapon). Different classes changes your playstyle whether your taking the enemies attention for youe teammates to deal damage or killing them with melee or ranged, there are some aoe options for ranged from the wizard, dwarf (drake pistol), merc (blunderbus) and elf (Hagbane).
Cons
Repititve
No custom maps
Only player hosted servers
Double special spawns (2 pinners at the same time for example, if the one before also spawn pinners and you didnt kill them that would be 4)
Only 2 game modes
Maps aren't balanced for loot (Some maps wont be played at all on higher difficulties)
Teleporting mobs (as host I can see them teleport from 10 meters away to me)
Specials spawning on you (about 3 times stormvermin patrols spawned on me across the span of 5 games(if you dont know stormvermin are tough armored rats which deal massive damage and are armored so you have to kill them with headshots or charged attacks)
Questionable optimization (not bad but certainly not good, goes from 90 fps to 15 at some parts of maps)
DLC are pretty expensive for what it gives (1 map for 3USD average)
No restart button
No way to select map after loot screen you have to go back to inn
Lots of bugs sometimes with patches
Half of the time daily missions for loot are locked behind dlcs
You can get overwhelmed easily when 2 of the same specials spawn at the same time at the same place as it essentially halves your team if you cant dodge. I feel it is rather improper way of spawning specials, they dont vary their spawns. Enemies teleporting is really bad but somewhat managable in certain ways. Now the bane of my life in this game, things spawning ON YOU. Like they just spawn a whole storm vermin patrol on you which basically says bye bye restart boy. Not being able to select what map you want after the loot screen is a little weird to me. Why do you have to go back to the inn and go through another loading screen? There is also no restart button, the only way to restart is to have the whole squad die. Patches come through with not much testing like the bug currently is being stuck in engines of war where you have to exit the game and let the bots teleport to get out, if your host and get stuck... well restart. Only having 2 game modes this games old pretty fast with only coop and survival to choose from. No custom maps at all means after playing a map 10 times makes it pretty old pretty fast (1 play through takes about 30mins to an hour depending on map)
Overall its a good game but it gets old amazingly fast, if you dont mind older games L4d2 would be a better bet, they even have tons of modded servers for a lot of unique gameplay.

Addictive, especially if you're a medieval building sim fan. There is a similarity with games such as Stronghold, Banished, or Kingdoms and Castles. What differentiates it from those however is the amount of detail comprised in its mechanics - the food and calories system, the preparations required for the upcoming winter etc. are all impressive gameplay components that feed the game's longevity.
My biggest complaint however is the balance: in the longrun it becomes almost impossible to sustain your villagers in a realistic manner - you can build as many bakeries as you want, slaughter as many chickens as possible, or plant a maximum amount of orchards, it will never be enough.
If those balance issues are fixed though, the game can be impeccable.

As many people have said, this is essentially Banished, there is no way around that, but it's a pretty decent Banished 1.5 so far, and seeing as that game hasn't seen any updating in some time, it's nice to have a version with improved graphics and interfaces, plus additional building types and terraforming functions.
Forest Village also allows you individual control of villagers (most importantly teenagers who aren't in your true workforce yet) so you can run food or supplies to specific buildings that the AI is ignoring for whatever priority reason. In Banished, if you had one or more buildings running out of food, you had to trust on the AI to supply that building at some point; with Forest Village, you can take control of an idling teenager, run to the woods and shoot a boar, grab the meat, and drop it off at whatever house needs it. Rinse and repeat until your food supply gets back in order.

Binary Domain is Sega's answer to Gears of War.  It's an over-the-top cover based shooter with a gallery of enemies to mow down.  While it doesn't win any awards originality it does have some pretty sweet boss encounters.  The story is a complete parody of bombastic action movies complete with strong stereotypes (the loud American, the black bruiser, the British jerk♥♥♥♥♥ even a French robot who wears a red ascot) and while it's completely groan worthy it's at least entertaining.
And that's the takeaway message here.  Binary Domain is completely arbitrary but entertaining.

Think of this as a B movie video game. The story is great, but very cliche until the very end. The combat is pretty common for a shooter, nothing amazing. I did have fun in the long run. There were some amazing boss fights and the art design was gorgeous.  Sadly the game has some big downsides that might scare people off. The major ones I ran into was with the controls. The game wouldn't let me remap left shift, and often it gave me the wrong button prompts during timed events. Finally there's a few auto scroller sections that you can tell were not made or changed at all for mouse and keyboard. One of the worst ones was with a speed boat. It tells you to use A and D to move left to right, but once pushing them it's not just a little move, but a drastic shift. Hit the walls too many times and you need to retry. I did this around 10 times before finding my brothers Xbox controller. First try with a controller I got it. You could lightly press left or right and move just slightly, unlike with A and D which are counted as full button inputs left or right.
Myself, I wish there was a Muh rating. I had fun and didn't totally hate it, but I wouldn't force people out to buy it. On the other hand it's not total trash and wouldn't tell anyone no if they did want to pick it up. Again think of it as a B movie. It's fun even with all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ parts.

Binary Domain…a game that has (for me personally) the best and the worst features in equal measures.
First of all I hate QTE’s with a vengeance and secondly I resent being channelled to the extent that I feel totally out of control of how I like to play my character and this game does this to the full extent.  I felt I was literally channelled through a straw most of the time.  After all the holding hands at every step I felt totally abandoned when it did let go.  This is definitely in the line of not being the puppet master but being the puppet.  Someone else is pulling the strings and once in a while these strings get cut like blink and you missed it.
Once I got over the fact that I can in no way play the game but only be part of it I got to enjoy the whole story, the crew members and the ever so well done background quite well.  The command voice feature was totally lost on me, more of a nuisance than helpful since I play as a lone PC user and therefore not particularly happy with multi player/Kinect aspects.  A different way of communication while in combat would have been better than finding the tab key and a hotkey.  Took me out of the battle in too many inconvenient situations, not cool to suddenly standing still in a hail of bullets to answer or direct your crew. The keyboard and mouse functions are ok and work quite well once I got used to them.
As a single player I liked the fundamental principles of having a choice of various different members of crew, very nicely done.  I could do with more single player games like that. The voice acting is very good; the crew is a nice bunch of various characters and backgrounds. Oh, …and a very …different kind of a french guy. The background story is very much japanese/futuristic/fantasy orientated which I didn’t mind at all.  It is a very over the top with everything game with lots of fun. Micromanagement is a combination of earning credits by destroying robots and by buying upgrades and items for everyone.
All in all a very nice little shooter with weapons and grenades and a good paced action with a little help from your crew members.  With a lot more in-game freedom  and  a little tweaking of the keyboard and mouse functions, this could have been a lot more enjoyable.  Maybe next time????  I sort of hope there will be more games like this since the emphasis on the new games coming out are way too much multi player orientated for me.

I would recommend to buy this game when on sale (as I did), it isn’t all too long, around 10 hours  plus worth of playing time.  Play it the first time on easy to get used to it and then play it through on the hard setting.  It is fun enough to replay it at various times, and that makes it recommendable in my eyes.

I got this from a bundle and I told myself why not?
Supreme League of Patriots is a episodic game with Kyle Keever, an American guy apparently working in NYPD (I still didn't gather what his role is as he's asked to type interviews but is referred as a janitor after), dreaming of being an actor..., mainly a super hero. With his British friend Mel, he's going to audition for a reality show...
While the graphics style is clearly indicating that you're in a parody à la Sam & Max, the way the characters are communicating is a reference to the comic super heroes world.
The core mechanics is a point-and-click. But I wish that the inventory/utility belt was easier to use. I mean, why should I open the inventory for combining items and use the utility belt to... use them in the scene? Being original is good. But being practical is also a good option. I was really confused at that. I would have prefer the combine option in the utility belt. Why? Because I can easily the utility belt by placing my cursor at the bottom of the screen instead of opening the top of my screen and make a click on the box to open the inventory.
Another gameplay problem is that you can easily obtain items... but can't use them before speaking to a character. Or the fire alarm puzzle. I didn't understand why, despite seeing people going out, in order for you not to have people look at your attempt to cheat, they've come back to the room and... you can make your trick with them present.
The dialogues, while funny, are, after a while, boring. I mean, yeah, Kyle is apparently an idiot. No need to remind it at every line. Besides, the characters are perhaps a cliché... and I have a problem with the Purple Patriot becoming suddenly the opposite of Kyle, who, despite his dumbness, is a real sweet and tolerant guy. Or with Melvin carrying around his Bristish bag like... well, sorry to me, but it seems weird.
But overall, unlocking achievements every 5 minutes.... Seriously? Unlocking an achievement at every sentence at the end of the game?
Yet, the game looks promising. I got the second episode thanks to the mini bundle on Groupees... I'll probably get the third episode later.
Give it a try. For the price, it's not a rip off.

I really didn't know what to expect from the game. When I found out it was point-and-click, I was kind of wary because I didn't like The Walking Dead... in it's defense, I played it on a console. A controller couldn't match the convenience of a mouse for these types of games. I've mainly played a few point-and-click classics. Maniac Mansion being a personal fave, and totally sucking at 7th Guest. Actually, that's it. Oh, and two of the Leisure Suit Larry games.
I started with the Tutorial, which helped a lot. I found the humor to be right up my alley (meaning I love it)! A good pop-culture reference here, gaming reference there, crude humor here, and I'm less than two hours in. The game is really based on dialogue, and the voice acting is really good. The voices are a pretty good match for the character designs and personalities. The closeups with mouth movement in sync with the audio makes the dialogue a little more lively. The game model is solid, and can be tedious. It's more a game of how much you are willing to put in will affect how quickly you will proceed. I've already been stumped a few times for not being more attentive.
Overall, it's a solid game, and I've only had a small sample size. I'm sure it will get better as I get further. I will definitely complete the three issues when I have time as I'm currently in the process of moving.
P.S. - Received the game free thanks to the generosity of No Bull Intentions. They went out of their way when they didn't have to over the Arkham Knight PC debacle. PC Gamers have to be seen as more than a niche market for studios. For what little it may do, I commend them for showing support for PC Gaming (and Gaming in general).

Dialogue and inventorying aside, Supreme League of Patriots is very much what you’d expect from an adventure game. A helpful task list makes sure you always know what you’re supposed to be doing to advance the plot, and the cheerful graphics and music make for a nice, uplifting (albeit sarcastic) storyline.
At the end of the day, No Bull Intentions has done a really nice job creating a humorous take on the point-and-click adventure and it’ll definitely be interesting to see how this studio progresses in the future. If you’re a fan of dialogue-heavy stories and trope-laden sarcastic asides, then Supreme League of Patriots might be worth your time.

Supreme league of Patriots:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Supreme league of Patriots is a point and click adventure in three episodes. As I finished the first episode “A Patriot is Born”, and thoroughly enjoyed it, here is a review based on the first one.
You will play Kyle (not the brightest character you’ll ever play), who is trying to enter the latest American Reality TV show, “America’s Got Super Powers,” as the Purple Patriot. His best mate, Mel who accompanies him at the audition, is an illegal alien in New York (just like “An Englishman in New York” from Sting, a fabulous song by the way) and has a fantastic and witty sense of humour.
The contrast between the two main characters really makes the game, in my opinion. You will also meet other very interesting characters, the likes of “The Cold War Warrior”, “Consuela” and the panel of judges who will give you plenty of surprises.
You will not have many difficulties in the puzzles but if you do, just speak with your counterpart and ask for his help; you will be pointed in the right direction.
The artwork is well done, a marvellous soundtrack and a fun story. It is refreshing to play a game that takes the mickey out of the society we live in!
Positives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Great artworks / Characters
-	Seriously funny dialogue
-	Fun Story
-	Achievements
-	Trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~~
-	Inventory system not so easy to use
I am looking forward to play the next two episodes.
I must warn you, you will experience outbursts of laughter playing this game!
8/10

Nice, funny point and click adventure game.  You play Kyle, a non-intelligent slacker who becomes an equally non-intelligent Republican super hero after taking too many blows to the head.  He is followed by his sidekick Mel, who is a British illegal alien.  There really aren't any puzzles that you will have much trouble with or a deep story to get into.  It is just a very linear piece with a lot of goofy humor spread throughout.  A lot of it seems a bit mean and very un-PC, but I enjoyed it.  It honestly seems more like a demo than an actual game.  It is VERY short.  I'm still giving it a thumbs up, but I wouldn't recommend paying 6 bucks for it.  Get it on sale if at all possible.  I doubt I will find out how the story ends since the other two chapters are the same price.  Each.  I really dunno why they released the game this way, but I'm not in the business so I have no reason to understand it.  Still, it is a funny little distraction.

Yet, I’ll recommend this game, with a strong suggestion to get it with a big discount only. This game’s humour is definitely not for everybody!

Im usually very picky when it comes to games and I was pretty spontaneous with this game especially with it being a random find but the game was amazing. The graphics are fantastic, everything has a lot of detail and the story itself was incredible. The concept of the game is so deep and I love games with such amazing stories. I played the game straight through from the moment I bought it and it took me about 8 hours to beat it, so its not a very long game but its not such a bad length for its price. Also the game has a few more endings and a lot of collectibles which I didnt get on my first run through so I will be playing it again. Unfortunately the game also does have a few downfalls. I have a regular Mac Book pro with no enhancements for gaming and playing the game on the highest quality was a bit rough with a bit of glitching throughout many parts in a couple levels, in fact the ending froze for me entirely which was very frustrating, so I would recommend playing the game on a slight lower setting, getting it on the console, or just playing it on a more prepared computer/laptop. Another thing that was disappointing was that the game has a lot of depth which is great but throughout my first play through I found myself with a lot of questions and very few answers and after a bit of reading about other experiences it didnt seem like a lot of people ended the game with many more answers than I, so Ive yet to purchase the DLC but it seems like it just might be a must in order to really understand. Last but not least, after my frustrating lag which resulted me missing the ending, I googled the endings and honestly, they could have been better. I felt like the entire time playing through the game I was building up for something intense and powerful and it just failed me. Nevertheless, the game was still an awesome experience and I really recommend it.

This is a really really good game. An homage to the whole horror survival genre with an awesome story that I enjoyed very much. It's like Kubrick's Shining with a mixture of a bit of Matrix and Inception. The gameplay is as good as it can be, I mean it's a survival horror game so you have to face challenges. Not just the bosses but basic things like getting ammunation, HP packs, or material to upgrade your skills. That means you will die a lot and a lot of situations can be really tough if you don't have enough ammo for example (or the other stuffs needed for the given part in the game). Also there is a good balance between stealth, running away, or straight up fighting against the enemy. That means sometimes you have to try several times to understand what the situation needs.
I bought the Season Pass too (thanks Summer Sale!) and I highly recommend to play the 2 story DLC as they explore the original story more and the might give you some answers for the unanswered questions. Or not :D Also the 1st DLC plays totally differently than the main game which is pretty cool tho I'm sure some people are not enjoying it. The 2nd one is similar to the main game, even introducing a new weapon (sawed off shotgun)!
So to me it's really hard to say anything negative about the game. Tho I have to mention the FOV and the letterboxing. You can't change the FOV but the letterboxing can be turned off. But don't do that. The whole purpose of having a small FOV and the letterboxing is to force the anxiety on the player. And I think it works really well. Sometimes I get nauseous if a game has a too small FOV but I didn't experience that in this game. Maybe the letterboxing helps on that as you only see the main protagonist from an above the hip camera angle all the time. Your mileage may vary but that was my experience.

Welcome to the Birthplace of Real-Time Turn Based Gameplay!  This is really going to catch on BIG TIME !!!
This kind of game has never been high up on my wish list but based on the Steam Videos and images alone I felt compelled to request a copy for review from the developers and thankfully they accepted.
For somebody like me, who has never even tried a role play card / board game (like wargames) I would have to put myself squarely into the complete Noob rank for a title like this.  However the controls were easy to pick up, harder to master and the game felt fun and challenging throughout.
I like the styling, the clever board look and feel and the in-game animations and audio create a brilliant atmosphere.
This is still EA and the devs appear to be communicating with the community and better still listening and eager to please.
For a title like this I don't really know what the *important* features might be but what I do know is that in my first look review
I absolutely understood why so many people play these games and why they get so involved with them too.
Now if this were using the traditional turn based approach (a genre I don't much like) I don't think it would have been my cup of tea but with the new style of gameplay `Real-Time Turn Based` it really sped things along and kept the game flowing and the pressure was always on too!  I like the strategy, the pace, the characters and the storylines....just brilliant all the way through.
Hands down this is a fantastic title with lots more to come and my word I might have found a new game to get my teeth into long term.

It's obvious that the developers of Vermintide were big fans of the Left4Dead franchise; while it would be unfair to call Vermintide merely a re-skin of that co-op classic, it bears the influence of Valve's game quite proudly and it is nearly impossible to review - or play - without making comparisons. Like Left4Dead, Vermintide is a four-player co-op shooter and many of its rat-men monsters bear a close correspondence to the varied forms of Valve's zombies. But Vermintide plays with this formula, adding a Team Fortress-like class-system, some light role-playing elements and a stronger campaign, all of which - on the surface - seems like some great additions. And - generally - they are; fans of the Left4Dead series will find a lot to like. Nonetheless, all this added extra chaff does take away from some of the addictive simplicity of the older title.
The worst offender were the maps, which are significantly larger than Left4Dead's levels but received far less iterative testing, as evidenced by the number of times I found myself inadvertently backtracking thanks to poor presentation of which direction I was supposed to head next. It didn't help that so much of the levels looked alike, an issue not assisted in the least by the gloomy grey graphics. The sheer size of the levels was problematic too; my interest waned long before the I got to the end of each map, and the lack of save-points meant that a total-party-kill required us to traverse the entire tedious map from the start. On the other hand, I did enjoy that the maps all had unique goals to them beyond merely surviving to the end.
Nor was I particularly warm to the class system, mostly because there wasn't enough difference between the classes. Yes, the Witch-Hunter was mainly a ranged-class that relied on his flintlocks, the Dwarf a melee tank, or the Bright Wizard a finicky glass cannon prone to overheating, but in actual gameplay all the classes were all focused on killing; there were no support classes, or healers or stealth classes. The RPG elements - mostly consisting of weapon unlocks as you level up - seemed mostly added as an excuse to make the players grind-up, extending the length of a game which had a dubiously small number of maps to begin with.
I mostly played in single-player and the AI was satisfactory, if lacking in the character and uniqueness that made Left4Dead's heroes so memorable. I did make a few excursions online and found the gameplay largely the same. While the community seemed largely friendly, Vermintide is more forgiving of soloing heroes, which reduced the need for co-operative play and a lot of the time the other players just seemed to run off and do their own thing. The game felt lonelier for that.
Vermintide is an acceptable clone of Left4Dead, but it lacks the polish of its obvious inspiration. The developers seemed to believe that "more" equaled "better" as evidenced by how they tossed in new gameplay elements almost wily-nily, but in doing so ruined the careful balance introduced in Valve's game. The end result was a rather shallow and unmemorable title and while Left4Dead had retained a position on my hard-drive for close to 8 years, I've no regret uninstalling Vermintide after a single month.
Nonetheless, I will grudgingly give this game my recommendation, because in the end it isn't terrible and - for fans of the co-op shooter genre - it will probably be a welcome addition to their libraries. For anyone else, though, there are better games available.
