Negatives:
♦ Little overpriced (I would only buy this on sale for like $3-5)
♦ No way to see Steam Friends Highscores or Other Players Highscores (They could easily implement this)
♦ Only one themed machine (They could easily implement different Machines for each worms game)
Overall, in my opinion, the game is fun, has all the classic worms sounds and acts just like you were on a real Arcade Pinball Machine and I love trying to beat my own highscores. However, without a way to see other peoples highscores or your Steam friends it is kind of lame. Also with only having one theme for the machine, it also makes it kind of lame. However, as this is still enjoyable to play a game here and there, to try and beat your own highscores, to enjoy some classic worms animations and sounds and just to relive the wonderful Arcade Pinball Machine experience... I'd recommend you buy this Pinball game if you loved Worms and Pinball!
Overall, I'd rate this 4/5!

My rule of thumb is that all games with effort into them are worth some amount of money. With that said, I still wish I hadn't bought the bundle this game came with. The story is minimal, but still interesting. Although, it's also never actually explained. Some will say "but you'll understand if you play the Cube Escape games!" but I say "Then it should be bundled with those game". Even then, any kind of side-game should still be even somewhat entertaining and understandable to some degree on its own. This game, isn't.
The puzzles range from actual brain-teasing to 100% random, to click-everywhere-until-something-happens-maybe. I enjoyed the puzzles that used legitimate logic, but some were either random and you had to find by accident, or completely betrayed the game's earlier use of logic. I won't spoil any of them, but by the time the end of the game came, the lack of closure or an actual story at all had me extra frustrated with the poor excuses for "puzzles" near the end of the game.
It's definitely easier, shorter, and more lacking in story than the other game in the bundle, Rusty Lake: Roots. But I personally regret purchasing both games. If you can get it for a dollar, buy it. If not, you can get the exact same experience watching someone play through it live.

Cat Quest is a simple but competently made, fun and charmingly designed Action RPG.
The visual design is very cute and in some ways rather clever. There are only the overworld, that looks like you are constantly traversing a big map, and simple dungeonmaps you go in fight everything and the leave again.
Some of the fun lies therein how the game plays with this aspect and uses it in humorous ways to lead the player around and from battle to battle, putting down lines and x and other symbols on it like it was drawn unto the world.
The Gameplay is VERY simple, quests are super linear and the fun in following them comes mainly from how the game presents the little scenarios and stories in.
The combat is quick and easy to understand, so easy in fact i wont go into details because after fighting just one enemy most people will have understood everything there is. HOWEVER that doesn't means the game can be beat by button mashing, not at all. Players who just mindlessly button mash and not pay attention to the warnings for incoming attacks will find themselves frequently and repeatedly dying.
The Equipment system is actually a bit broken. You find equipment in form of hats/helmets, armor and weapons and if you have a specific item again said item will be upgraded. There are chests to find in the world but you can only find and loot them once. After that you need to rely on the smith. In the smithy the player can choose to purchase a small chest for 50 Gold or a big chest for 5000 gold. The Items out of that are randomly chosen and then upgrade their respective gear in your inventory.
This sadly leads to some of the items being flat out useless although they might look better since you have a chance that they never are going to be better then the ones you got a the beginning and that you leveled up big time until then.
Never has a game more needed a fashion slot more so that the players can equip the look they want while getting the stats from something better.
The magic system is okay, nothing special but also usefull enougzh so that you constantly use it.
Now, to be truthfull, the game is actually really repetetive when it comes to its gameplay.
You pick up a quest, you follow the marker, kill a bunch of enemys and then follwo the next marker. That is all there is to it.
That i still recommend it comes from the fun stories presented in the quests and main line and the light humor of its design overal.as well from the fact that it is rather short.
After 13 hours i played trough the main quest, all sidequests and several quests you need to discover trough exploration.
There are a few highlevel tasks still over as well as some REALLY Highlevel Dungeons that i feel are only there if your REALLY want to grind more in this combat.
The game wont blow your mind.
But Cat Quest doesn't outstay its wellcome and until its end is well made, well presented and fun to play.

The Evil Within tries very hard to be Silent Hill, but plays like a Resident Evil. I know I only have six hours of play time, but hear me out. I couldn't bring myself to finish it, it was so frustrating.
Pros:
-Looks great. Awesome visuals, monsters and level themes.
-Sounds pretty good. Really gritty, crunchy, gut-wrenching sounds and visceral combat effects.
-Story is interesting, but doesn't really hook you with anything that you want to figure out. It's more a collectible hunt than a narrative mystery.
-Melee combat is hectic and satisfying, and ranged combat is kept as a last resort with limited ammo.
Cons:
-The writing is medicore at best. None of the characters are interesting, the dialogue is questionable and the in-game journals look like they were written by a high-schooler.
-The crossbow has an effective range of three feet. When the primary ammunition is explosive, you're usually better off firing it ahead of you and using it like a land mine.
-Stealth is broken, in the sense that it only works half the time. There are several scripted encounters where the enemies will react to your presence whether or not you are sneaking, and they are surrounded by other enemies that you can sneak around. In fact,
it's completely impossible to tell who will immediately attack you and who can be avoided.
-Enemies are inconsisent. When you first encounter an enemy, he's invincible and it's clear you're not supposed to fight him. The next time you find him, you're supposed to fight him. Or you'll find a special monster surrounded by ammo, and it will stagger and collapse when you attack it, but it's actually invincible and you're supposed to run away.
-Navigation and camera work are abysmal. I've spent more than one fight with the camera literally INSIDE my butt, and I've had to shuffle along fences trying to find a break in the invisible wall to hop over a two foot obstacle.
-The "puzzles" are an insult to your intelligence. Skyrim had more challenging puzzles.

Long story short: the good horror game is in the demo. The rest feels like a crossover between RE4 an SH: Homecomming writen by tentacle hentai horror doujinshin writer too much into hollywood action movies and not that much into sex or horror of any kind. The graphics are great, but poorly optimized in comparison to other games of the same kind and time with a bad taste design.
I have to inform you, that I'll compare this game A LOT to RE4, and unlike most I HATE RE4. Don't take it wrong, RE4 is not that bad a game. It's actually a reasonable action game and a very original one at the time of its release but a bad Resident Evil and a awfull Horror Game, and its flaws as an Horror Game (or Survival Horror for that matter) are magnified in The Evil Within.
So. I've finally finished this game and I can't recommend it to anyone looking for an good exclusively action, stealth or horror game. Although The Evil Within is not a bad game per se, the same way as RE4, it suffers from being a Duck. The duck can fly, the duck can walk, and the duck can swim, but none of those with any grace.
The Evil Within is clearly a game that suffered from it's great ambitions. It doesn't cut as an Action Game. You'll find weapons and ammo enough to shoot and kill almost every enemy you can, and have some spare to shoot some enemies that can't be killed - at normal difficulty and lower - but its clumsy. You can aim, but the camera zooms toó much and moves too far away from the character, leaving you in situations were enemies that seems to be close enough and in position to be point blank shoot, but will be missed, because the crosshair clearly is not doing its job.
The camera will also always stick to your right side when not crouching, making it impossible to find and shoot things that are in a hallway to your left. Crouching also doesn't help because you can't shoot while crouching, except for throwing bottles to distract enemies.
Inventory management feels weird. Ammo doesn't occupy a place or slot, but you're limited to a short amount per weapon. But you'll collect quite a few weapons during the game, making the purpose of ammo rationing quite useless unless in harder difficulties. If you aim well enough to kill an enemy fast and have spare ammo for the next, you'll never have an inventory empty, nor full.
Enemies fall onto two groups: zombies and bosses.
Zombies will behave almost exactly like their RE4 older cousins, except that a headshot will not kill them unless you've completely cut their heads off. I missed this part of biology classes but apparently the brain is truly located in the lower part of the jaws.
Bosses on the other hand have no brains. Headshots don't do greater damage and one of them (or two?) is actually invulnerable from headshots. Their design also is uninspired for both bosses and zombies, ranging from zombie that fell on barbed wire to ripoffs and mashups from famous franchises and myths such as Samara from The Ring had a daughter from Goro (MK), Pyramid Head from SH2 with a safe covering his head and a small sledgehammer, a mutilated spin of the classic Cerberus - the Three Headed Dog, and many others.
The AI is dumb, and once they notice your presence will just rush towards you mindlesly. Most of the bosses do the same, and although not that hard, most have an 1-hit-kill attack. So if you miss something once: you're dead!
The Evil Within doesn't cut as an Stealth Game. One of its biggest selling points is that stealth is a great deal, and the environment plays a great role in dealing with enemies. But almost half of the traps don't affect anyone other than you, or if they affect, are never placed in zones with other enemies. Other traps just cannot be sneaked over, and work only as a door that you have to stop and open.
Many levels force you into combat in the end, kind of killing the point of stealth.
If you're really into it, you can activate a detection alert, that shows you when enemies are searching for you or have already found you, but it only work with enemies that are close enough so that you're almost sure to kill him, or will on some rare cases it may give you signs of life from enemies that are only found later in the game, but their rooms a right on the other side of the wall besides you. Many enemies spot you when you enter the room and attack you instantly, or will act like haven't spotted and kill you in a 1-hit-kill trap.
Environmental traps show a sh***y design choice. Many only exist in one place, once in the game, and if you're not watching for a game that's trying to f*** with you, they're first presented by killing you! It really kills the mood.
Lastly, The Evil Within doesn't cut as a Horror Game. Every mechanic in the game is present so that a player that has mastery with it will fell empowered by their control of the environment. And mastery removes the fear, the horror and the terror that a game like The Evil Within was supposed to provide. Same as RE4.
Their mechanics rewards me as a player for going against what brings those feelings in the game. Weapon Upgrades can be bought with a currency called green gel, that is largely rewarded from killing enemies, although possible to acquire solely from explorarion. By forcing me into combat I, as a player will grow used to them and in turn won't be afraid of them anymore. Take a game like Dead Space where upgrade points are only found through exploration and instead of forcing you into combat to progress and the difference is clear. Here I'm forced to explore and face a fear a lot harder to overcome: the fear of the unknown. The unknown dies really fast in The Evil Within, and the only mistery to be explored is "how will this game try to kill me next".
That become a problem of its own, a first time player will die so much that soon every passage becomes a repetition. Progressing in this game feels more like a Rythm Game than an horror game instead of making you afraid, every action becomes mechanic.
But what kills it in The Evil Within is the story. Spoiler alert:

Tha makes the game a bad sequence of being throwed around a nightmarish place that makes no sense up until the main protagonist states as clear as broad daylight what's going on, right around the middle of the game. After that point everything loses interest, because there's no more bad surprise, just a bad excuse for a story waiting you in the end.
What the game really does well is its graphics. Altough poorly optimized in comparison to others of the same period, and the unispired designs discussed previously, the game is beautiful, Models, textures, lighting and particles are outstanding.
And that's it.

This game is a great mesh of RPG and MMO gameplay features. Depending on which faction you choose (Federation, Romulan, Klingon), you start off as a low-ranking dude in their respective space fleets and then rise up the ranks. You can also choose between three classes: Science, Engineering, and Tactical, with each having its own unique benefits. The game puts you in charge of your very own ship, which you can customize to fit your liking (in addition, a wide range of customization options are available for your character). The game also allows you to upgrade character skills of both you and your team. Speaking of which, you can have your very own bridge team and away team who can help you in space battles and ground conflicts. I like how this game doesn't constrain you to your spaceship like some other sci-fi games, and also allows you to beam to space stations and mission locations.
This game is fantastic, offers a vast variety of features and stuff I haven't fully explored yet, and would suit sci-fi fans. Like the Star Trek TV series and movies, this game carries a theme of exploration and I really think this game carries that across. Although I grew up loving Star Wars, I think this game has made me love the Star Trek universe too. I see myself putting many hours into this heck of a game.

Rusty Lake Hotel is highly reminiscent of those old Flash "Escape the Room" games. You find yourself at hotel where all of the other guests are various animals. Your goal: murder each guest and serve them for that night's dinner. Crazy and weird theme, but interesting nonetheless. The game is simply a series of room puzzles, where you click around to find items, combine these items or use them in the environment, and solve occasional puzzles that eventually lead to the death of your chosen guest. These types of games often suffer from "moon logic", where players can get stuck due to illogical item combinations, but fortunately Rusty Lake Hotel is pretty straight forward.
I personally really enjoyed Rusty Lake Hotel. It's a humble game: simple and short, but engaging and with an appropriate pricetag. For people looking to scratch that "escape room" itch or just want to kick back with a weirdly disturbing game, this should be right up your alley.

Layers of Fear is a
psychological horror game with always-climbing fear and suspense that puts you in the place of an artist, who bears some mental disorder (schizophrenia?) and returns home to finish his masterpiece.
As you walk about your huge mansion, you will begin to notice very horrific changes in both the environment, scenary, and of course, the paintings themselves as you uncover the dark secret behind this artist's past and his deranged mind.
At every corner, there are jumpscares, "should-I-go-in-there-or-not" moments, as well as persistent and ever-increasing states of fear that continue to form as you progress through both the storyline of the game and the game itself.
The game is pretty short: only 6 Chapters, but many things happen in each chapter, making the game rich of fear, yet full of anxiety and excitement to endure:D.
For the sake of achievements, there are mementos and family items that one can find in this game, further immersing oneself in the background of this mad artist, while also understanding what happened to him and his family.
Graphics are truly amazing in this game, so well established and detailed that my eyes become dragged to the screen everytime I see paint, or a chair, or pretty much anything in this game. No joke, one can observe the texture of the paintings themselves as if one was right where the artist is, and one can see the detail of the walls, plants, windows, and surrounding environment (walls, floor, furniture, etc.) [Kudos to the devs that made such an excellent game].
The music on both the starting of the game and in the game is very harmonic, in fact, brings scary ambience to the game and its own environment.
In addition, one can choose to continue along the story path or the optional route, bringing an the artist into deeper, scarier parts of his mansion to uncover either more mementos or darker secrets, providing this game with interesting opportunities as well as becoming immune to a "path-driven" game with a dull one-route guide.

I feel like I have to write this review after seeing how much hate this game recieved from gamers and reviewers.
I also played all 3 DLCs and got the fighting chance pack (no I did not preorder). I bought this game when it was on sale for roughly 15 dollars. After doing everything possible in the game, I can tell you that THIS GAME iS VERY WELL MADE. It is more of a tribute to every famous horror game out there.
It seems that most haters are those people who wanted this game to be a jumpscare horror game that also resembled Resident Evil (4 in this case). Yes I agree this game is not scary, however it does give you an uneasy feeling going through the levels which are rewarding and not repetative. Further more like Resident Evil, it is a SURVIVAL HORROR FIRST. Let's face it those people who are constantly praising RE4 (I'm one of them) and hating this game, don't seem to realize that RE4 had the exact same "problems" as this game; it was also not scary, more adventurous, with lots of unerving elements, and somewhat questionalbe dialogue and AI. I for one think this game went in a better direction because it eliminated "funny" cringe-worthy one-liners that RE4 had.
As for the plot (which appears to be the second main reason people hate this game), honestly I had no trouble analysing the plot. Yes, it is confusing, and cliche at times, but the more you think about it the more it makes sence. Look at the main plots from RE series or even Silent Hill series; they are also confusing as hell most of the time. My advise for those who have trouble with the plot, just look at from this perspective: You play as the detective Castellanos, therefore you only see what he sees, no one is going to hold your hand so that you will understand whats going on. It is very difficult to make a strong plot for any game, and Horror games are the most difficult to come up with a good plot.
All and all, do not let bad reviews discurage you from playing this game.

First time I tried the game in 2014 I was lukewarm towards it at best and intensely disliked it at worst. Primarily, because of the seemingly nonsensical story.
All the doubts I had concerning the story in the base game were gone with DLCs (The Assignment and The Consequence), which I now played for the first time. What needs to be mentioned is that the explanations for the events taking place are not contrived in any way and shed some light on the mindset of the developers - they had the story all planned out, but decided to leave a lot of the elements in the dark to make it, I guess, more mysterious or open to interpretation. While it does make sense to omit the background events if one decides to tell the story purely from the perspective of the main character (Sebastian), it backfired by making it seem a boring, unoriginal rehash of ideas presented in an overcomplicated, incomprehensible way. However, the DLCs fix this by clearing nearly everything up, but still leaving enough questions unanswered for a potential sequel. The story turned out to be actually pretty good, fairly complex and well told (though the characters still fall flat). What's more, it made me care about the universe and be hopeful for a continuation.
The Executioner DLC is a fun distraction - after being hunted by boogeymen, now you ARE the boogeyman.
As for the rest of the game - it attempts to fuse Silent Hill and Resident Evil - the symbolism of creatures and travelling through diamensions of SH with the gameplay and some of the locations of RE. At first I hated it, but now I ask myself, why not? Why should SH be the only series of games that attempts heavy symbolism with its monstrosities? The Evil Within does it fairly well. Not as good as SH, but still. Gameplay wise it can be rough around the edges (the camera can be annoying, control of the character is not as responsive as I would like, a bit too many insta-kill enemies), however one can get used to it.
Horror wise - the base game is not scary, but the two DLCs (The Assignment and The Consequence) are a lot slower paced (they focus on stealth above all else) and can be frightening. However, in all instances, the game succeeds at creating an environment where, no matter where you find yourself, you never feel safe - there is always that lingering, uncomfortable feeling present at all times.
All in all I think The Evil Within has great sequel potential and, with enough polish, it can easily rival the best in the genre.

Okay, The Evil Within is a decent game. It does not excel but it does its job well. Its a pretty standard Japanese horror game. I say this like I've played lots of them, I haven't. But think Silent Hill/Resident Evil and you get the clue. Foul creatures, the stuff of nightmares. Characters that are way too deep in the uncanny valley. Mind♥♥♥♥s everywhere and some kind of story that works more as a springboard for nightmare creatures than to actually trying to immerse you.
You play as Sebastian Castellano, a man who looks like he could drink all night, get into a couple of bar fights with local hobos and still look handsome enough to hit on your mom afterwards. He acts as the nightmare he is trapped in is only slightly worse than his regular life and shrugs of things that no normal guy should shrug off. He also shoots up health potions like a heroin addict and plays along with all the weird♥♥♥♥♥♥like he really doesn't care.
We also meet his partner, some nerdy guy who freaks out and wear gloves all the time, total serial killer vibes. There is also a girl, tough as nails and with a mission. We also got an evil doctor and some autistic child.
If this review seems hard to follow and unnecessary "all-over-the-place", but you are still reading this because of the colorful language and it you don't got anything else to do, well, then this game is for you.
The combat is satisfying, getting upgrades are fun and lighting people on fire is always fun. Sometimes it's positively creepy. The environments are sometimes immersive, but they tend to be predictable. The terror of being chased is real, and you're always on the brink of not having enough health and ammo.
If you’ve played games like Silent Hill and Resident Evil and enjoy them. This game is for you.

You're going to see a "No" from me on this when all is said and done. I love Star Trek. When I get the itch to fly one of the Federation-style ships around, this is unfortunately what scratches it these days.
The game has come quite a long way since release. Unfortunately, most of the missions are still following this formula:
Fly in space + fight lots of ships + scan 5 things + beam to one thing + fight lots of aliens + beam up + fight "boss" ship = STO mission.
Now, this formula is peppered with some more Star Trek flair - old, canon locations, voice actors and likenesses from the show and more robust and varied environments. Unfortunately, it's still the formula that gets repetitive and old rather quickly. I was certainly tired of it after the 70 hours I put in over summer break. I've met some nice people in game, but there is also the division of "Pay2Win" and "Free2Play" players within the game.
One day, Trek Diplomacy and Exploration mixed with realistic ship to ship combat will come. One day. That day isn't here yet, and STO isn't, nor appears in coming expansions, to be it.

So, say what you like about the various iterations of the show; I am personally quite a big fan of the many Star Trek series that have run from the sixties to now. That said, this game tends to favor the very grind-heavy approach that plagues games in the genre.
Space combat is its chief draw, and it's actually pretty fun. The way they represent the systems and flavor of everything is very Star Trek in design. It's the thousands of hours of missions and instances you need to run that put a damper on things. Outside of this, it is a simplistic system, and I gravitate towards FTL (if you like indie titles) or EVE (if you like hating yourself) for more depth.
Ground missions are all very combat-centric and I don't feel represent the brand as well as they could (take this with a grain of salt, the plot is focused on a huge quadrant-spanning war, to begin with).
Granted, I never reached endgame, so go ahead, give it a try!

I saw many people comparing this to Banished. I have never played Banished, so I cannot do that. What I did play though, was the Anno series, and I must say that this game reminds me a lot of those games. Sadly, minus the fun.
What bothers me most about it is that there is no clear goal, no competition, no interaction with other players (an AI would be fine for me), nothing. There is no reason for me to expand my village, because my villagers do not want things. *I* do not want things.
There are no quests, no enemy, no cool shiny thing that I get at the end. While this may be okay for some people, it is extremely frustrating for me. Why should I expand?
In the mentioned Anno for example, you have opponents. You have several islands and other players/AI, and if you don't expand fast enough, someone else will have claimed the island you wanted. The materials are split to those islands, you need to expand and make several settlements to keep your people happy, because you can not grow everything on every island. In Life is Feudal, however, your villagers are also happy with just fish while living in a simple hut.
Once you discovered the two or three extra kinds of animals or plants, you can build them on your island. But why? Simply because you can build something, does not make me want to build it. It feels like a very stripped down version of the mentioned game to me, and sadly, Life is Feudal adds nothing new. Sure, you can jump into your people, but that felt more like a useless gimmick to me.
I found Life is Feudal fun to play for about 6 hours. By then, I had not seen it all yet because the game is pretty slow, but I have absolutely no motivation to play on, which is a sad thing because initially, I liked it.

HuniePop is exactly what it says it is, a dating simulator. You will have the opportunity to meet different girls and socialize with them. (Just don't use what you learn in this game during a real life date)
You play as yourself. You are terrible at socializing with girls. One day, a magical fairy named Kyu shows up and decides to help you out.
The girls are pretty diverse. There are girls who are kind and passionate like Tiffany, and then there are girls who are haughty and loud like Audrey. All of them are actually well voice acted, making them feel "real".
HuniePop generally consists of talking and getting to know the girls you meet and going on a date with them. The dating scenes are pretty much what most people call "Bejewled".
However, I'd say HuniePop's gameplay is a bit "more fun" since you can match orbs horizontally or vertically (the orbs you want to match don't have to be next to each other). There's also a catch. You can't just match random colors and just win.
Ex: You want to date Tiffany. Her favorite trait is flirtation (a green token). When you are dating her, you will only have a certain amount of moves to fill up a point meter. Matching green tokens will get you the most points.
In addition to the "Bejewled gameplay, you can match bell tokens to get more moves and avoid the shattered purple hearts (They will decrease the meter).
Unless you install the uncensored patch, Panties and bras will stay on, but moans of pleasure will still be heard. :3
For people who just want a casual game that involves "Bejeweled" gameplay and dating girls, pick this up if you feel like it. You might find that one girl that you admire the most.

I could waste an hour or two playing this quite contently. But the fact that it's $8 by itself is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You can download Pinball FX2 right now on Steam for $0 and get one table for FREE. That table has online leaderboards, it'll tell you your controls, you can use a controller, and it has multiple camera angles, AND you can get extra tables for $3 for one or $10 for four. Worms Pinball would be fairly priced at a dollar or two. But $8 is ludicrous. If you can get it for a buck in a bundle, I can recommend it.

At some point in time, Worms reached the stage all games starring anthropomorphic characters do: the casual/sports spin-off period. Or at least Team17 seems to have thought it reached that point, because over the years they have been releasing various games in the Worms series which are not in fact anything like the core Worms games. Among these is Worms Pinball, which as the title would have you believe, is a pinball game themed around the characters and themes of franchise.
I don't feel I need to explain how to actually play pinball (that should be common knowledge), as the real question is "is this a GOOD pinball game?" The answer to that is, maybe when it was originally released, but not anymore. In the over a decade long span between then and now, digital pinball has improved exponentially and left Worms in a painfully dated time capsule of what pinball games used to be like. The laughable physics, inhibiting camera angles, and single table to play on are typical of the time it was released, but now that isn't anywhere near good enough.
If it was drastically cheaper, there is a small part of me that would recommend this to huge Worms fans as a mildly amusing novelty, but at its current price it feels like an insult. With so many other, far better pinball games to choose from (Pinball FX2 and Pinball Arcade come to mind), there is no reason to so much as glance at Worms Pinball. As far as Worms goes, this is one game that should have stayed in the ground.

I got hyped for the development of this game. I very recently started checking out Youtubers ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ themselves playing horror games. I thought this would be an excellent opportunity to actually play a game like this without seeing a series on someone's channel doing it for me. I loved the graphics, the story is alluring and I jumped into it with both feet.
But honestly, reading a book would be a quicker way to a satisfying horror experience. Huge pacing and space problems; everything felt extremely tedious and longwinded. The main character's game-long limp felt symbolic of how much I felt like I was dragging my feet. Oh, it's beautiful, and it gets the descent-into-madness landing perfect, slowly realizing how screwed up who you're playing as is, and his fall from grace into disgusting, monstrous psychopath... UGH IT'S SO GUD.
I'm not crying about a lack of jumpscares, or quality of. I knew I was, and wanted to get into a story-centric exploritory game without the overdone hide-n-seek or survival elements. There's a little of that but tastefully done.
I'm not a big fan of manual everything. Leave it in for the puzzles and primary objects involved with the story. AND THE SHEER VOLUME OF THESE EMPTY BOXES.
In the beginning of the game, the first walkthrough of the house is chock full of clues and hints to who you're playing, who lives in the house, things that happened, etc. In the puzzle areas, there's usually a clue, or two, which are stashed in a few cupboards. At least make them click(or press key)-to-open, so I can scan through them in a flash.
Better yet, don't put 20-40 little drawers and doors to fiddle with that are locked or have nothing in them but ambient objects you see plenty of times.
It distracts from the atmosphere and the story. Anyone who's played one of these exploration horror games knows you can miss a LOT of story, scares,
. So, throwing a heap of interactable objects is going to torture every completionist, lore-hungry gamers like myself. I'm staring at every surface already, why a horde of empty boxes, too? If I didn't know better I'd say it was to rack up extra gameplay hours. And I definitely missed half of the collectables simply because of fatigue.
/rant

The videos and screenshots make it look like Layers of Fear is an interactive horror film, one that makes use of the usually effective trope of warping reality -- walk down a hallway and see a door that wasn't there before, look up and see a benign painting suddenly leap to life with a malicious figure glaring down at you, step into an art studio and see a painting dissolve before your eyes.
Plenty of horror films have gotten great mileage out of that technique, skillfully combining it with a moody atmosphere and mounting sense of dread. A good example is the movie Grave Encounters, when the characters try to find the exit leading out from an abandoned psych hospital only to realize the building itself is changing, and won't let them leave. Or the evil force in 1408, which tortures John Cusack by letting him believe he's finally found a way out, only to snatch it away at the last instant.
But to do that effectively, the game has to establish a spacial baseline. In other words, we (the players) need to get a sense of place, a sense that we're inhabiting this creepy old mansion before things start changing. We have to know what the mansion looks like, and understand its basic floor plan, otherwise there's little point (or scares) in reality reshaping itself around  us.
Unfortunately, Layers of Fear doesn't let you do that -- it starts warping practically everything in the environment around you, constantly, wearing out the gimmick almost immediately and turning the whole experience into a linear walking simulator where there's nothing unexpected, because the unexpected is always happening.
Walk into a room, turn around and see a painting has changed, or a fireplace is now lit, or something appears out of thin air along with a dramatic orchestral stab. Walk through the door into another room, open some drawers, find a key, open the next door, find yourself in a weird hallway, open the next door...
This is a case of a good idea that was poorly executed, and it very quickly becomes boring.
Also, fair warning -- there's a looped piano riff that repeats from the start menu all the way through the first section of gameplay, and it quickly becomes grating, to the point where I had to shut the music off within the first 5 minutes of playing. That's never a good sign.
And YMMV, but this game gave me a headache. I think it has something to do with the camera movement and the awkward character movement. I had to stop playing after 40 minutes or so.
Verdict: Save your money and check out the many other more worthy horror titles on Steam. This game looks impressive in screens and videos, but it's an enormous letdown.

I first wrote this review in early access, but it is now UPDATED as of 2017-03-17
Ratz Instagib is a no-b*llsh*t, super fast-paced shooter where anyone can jump in and learn how to play in seconds. At the same time, the gameplay is almost completely skill-based and your aiming and movement skills (which can take weeks or months to master, especially the aim) directly determine the outcome of the game.
The game mechanics are as simple as it can get: you only have one weapon, the railgun, which is a one hit kill and you can boost in any direction (kind of like a rocket jump) by right clicking. The enemy hitboxes are extremely small and movement is extremely fast, which means that you have to be really good at aiming to hit your enemies.
Pros:
+ Very fast paced gameplay
+ Balanced, competitive gameplay
+ Responsive and smooth controls
+ Lots of customizations in the options menu (enemy colors, beam color, nickname color, X and Y mouse velocity, and a ton of other graphical options).
+ Performance is pretty good even though the game is made in Unity. I'm getting ~300-400fps on a i7-4790k and Sapphire r9 270x running at 1920x1080@120hz, I'd never expect an unity game to run so fast.
+ Multiple gamemodes
+ User-made workshop maps
+ Now allows connecting to a custom server
Cons:
- Could've included non-instagib gamemodes with the standard arena fps weapons and pickups
I highly recommend this as it's a lot of fun and also a great aim warm-up for games like Quake.

This is an escape room. Plain and simple. A computerized game version of an escape room. It seems like an adventure game and the mechanics match point and click adventures for sure. But it shuts you up in several rooms and you can't get out until you reach the room's goal. It's very creepy actually, telling an Agatha Christielike parlor room mystery of sorts. All the ladies and gentry are there. But all played by anthropomorphic animals. It all kinda works. And that makes it more odd. More creepy. And being animation they can crank up the weirdness a bit. Not the negatives....I guess flash is okay, but note it will give you warning messages telling you it is affecting your computer until you let it. Not SUCH a terrible thing I suppose. It does save its checkpoints. The only really frustrating thing I've hit in the gameplay is...well sometimes you don't know just what you are supposed to click. WHich makes you just click random places everywhere. Which is kinf od a fault with the adventure genre to begin with. No different here, especially when some of the puzzles aren't really puzzles but more "you can't move forward in the story and get THIS object until you talk to that person across the room", which has no logic whatsoever. Still...this is insanely cheap...and I'm glad I found it. Most games for 99 cents are total garbage. I think there is a series of these Rusty Lake games. THis is the first one I played. The second I don't like as well. It doesn't have animals and weird murders. In fact the murder mystery aspect is exactly what sells this game as an escape room. Even though there's no time limit you feel the urgency and the story. The other just plods along waiting for you to do things with no real link. This has a narrative. The rabbit magician coming out of his own magic hat is my favorite.

A creepy and eerie game. It is so sinister but it draws you in and compels you to complete the game. If you have ever played escape the room games then this is going to scatch that itch. It really helps to play some of the free games by Rusty Lake online to get the background story behind these characters but it is not necessary. Overal a wonderful game.

I only have about 10 hours in the game, but the average time to complete each level (25 levels, plus the prelude and a secret level) is about, lets say twenty seconds (if you don't die a billion times, which I probably did). If you times 25 (or 27 for specifics) by 0.20, then you'd get a total of 5 (or 5.4), which symbolizes 5 hours (I think so anyways). That would mean that I have plenty of time in-game to beat it damn near twice. (for extra math fun, multiply 27 by 2 to account for the hard mode that I'm currently attempting to complete) Enough with this, lets get to the actual review, in easy to read Pro & Con format.
PROS:
- First off, the soundtrack for this game is absolutley beautiful, in a synthwave tecnho way.
- Though irritating as hell sometimes, the gameplay is really fun.
- The story is pretty good, with 7 different storylines with alternating characters each with a unique playstyle.
- A scoring system (which is a grade, such as the classic A, B, C, D and F with respective + or - markings.) that entices players to play levels again to get higher scores.
- (on an unrelated note) The developers nerfed Tony so that he can't use weapons.
- A level editor, 'nuff said.
CONS:
- This game is hard as hell, death is very, VERY common. (though not really a con if you like hard games)
- The ending is a giant middle finger to players, leaving a bad taste of cliffhanger in the player's mouth.
- On that note, Dennaton Games will never make a third Hotline Miami, but they gave us a sweet level editor (released on December, 2015)
In the end, Hotline Miami 2 is a really good game, definetly worth the $15(ish) it costs. Nice job, Dennaton.

I recently purchased this game at the time of writing (8th February 2016) in the Lunar New Year Sale. I have not played very much (evident by my playtime) but have a basic grasp on the gameplay and how the game works, enough to write a review of decent length.
I bought this game on an impulse buy seeing how cheap it was. I only briefly glanced at the reviews, they were mostly short and there wasn't much to go on. I aim to correct that. Dead6hot is a retro-styled 2D platformer mixed with fighter and shooter elements. I do enjoy platformers, fighters and games with a retro art direction, but this will not add bias to my review.
Gameplay:
The gameplay is fairly simple. There are two modes, Singleplayer and Multiplayer. At the time of writing, I have not tried Multiplayer, as there is no online mode and I have no one to play with at this moment. Multiplayer is local multiplayer, not requiring an internet connection on your device to play. Multiplayer and Singleplayer both include the Versus mode, which is a generic fight between two characters. There are 5 stages to pick from, all with varying layouts. On top of this, there are 10 different characters, ranging from a clown to a minotaur. In Versus Mode, it is a 1v1 match, where both characters have 3 lives.
The character you use can run left and right, and also can jump, but doesn't have a mid-air double jump. Your character starts off with a pistol and a special (as far as I can tell this changes depending on which character you use). However every weapon in this game does have an ammunition limit. It is impossible to leave the stage, as going off the sides will bring you out it's opposite (the left side with bring you out on the right side, and the bottom will make you fall from the top, and vice versa). Item crates appear occasionally on stages, allowing you to get a new weapon to swap your current one with or to refill the ammo of the weapon in use. The controls for Player 1 use the arrow keys to control your movement, the L key to fire your weapon and the O key to use your special. As far as I am aware, these cannot be changed. Each character can only use 3 specials at one time. Health packs also spawn on the stages, allowing you to completely refill the health bar, which is located in the top corners of the screen. CPU ability levels can also be changed, from Timid, then onto Split, then Aggro.
The other mode that is found is simply called Singleplayer or Co-Op. The name changes depending whether you are playing in Singleplayer or Multiplayer. You pick a stage and character as normal, but when the game begins, it is more of a platforming side. You are fighting multiple enemies. One is a small slime, which spanws the most frequently, while the other is a floating eye, which is taller. The CPU enemies do not have weapons for themselves, and can only hurt your character by touching them. If your character falls on top of an enemy, you will still take damage. You are tasked with surviving as long as possible and killing as many enemies as possible too. There is no timer for any of the modes in Dead6hot
Pros:
- A good selection of different character designs.
- Great art direction and style for the game.
- Enjoyable and not frustrating for the user to play.
- Set at a good price.
Cons/Improvements To Be Made:
- Characters are no different in abilities and movement. It would be good to differenciate between each character and not make the different choices purely astethic.
- Weapon and stage choices are limited. It would be amazing if you could improve the roster of both.
- Health packs are very overpowered. They need to be reduced in the amount they can heal, or matches can become almost impossible to win and will last forever.
- There isn't a button to exit the game as of yet. That is a feature that needs to be implemented; the only way to exit the game right now is to press Alt+Enter and close the game.
- There is no online multiplayer. It would be a great addition and is almost required for a game of this style to thrive. If it is implemented, it will appeal to people who don't have others to play with.
Glitches Found:
- This has been confirmed as a glitch but was kept in because the game wasn't meant to be very serious. When I have been playing Singleplayer mode, I have found that jumping on top of an enemy can send you at least twice as high as normal jumping. I can't tell whether it is due to the damage system or simply a glitch due to collision boxes or maybe even something completely different.
Extra Points To Note:
- It feels like the controls for the stage and character selection are backwards. This may be a deliberate design choice, but the movement doesn't seem right to me.
Conclusion:
Overall, I enjoy this game. The creators have done a great job in capturing the feel of a retro game with the art style and soundtrack. The gameplay features are working and strong. There are quite a few things that can be improved, but the developers (Ridhwann Patel, Chuck Obrien and Tanner Daniels, as well as collaboration with New Reality Games) have a very good work-in-progress Steam game on their hands that I will play for hours as new updates come out. I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys platformers, fighting games, shooter games and retro-styled games.
I will be updating this review when new updates come and if I find something new with the game.

If you like chilling and steadily devolping a tiny group of settlers into a burgeoening, veritable metropilis of medievel wonders, this is for you. It's still being developed, but most of the game is pretty well polished. Pathfinding is a bit wonky, but can be worked around (leave your citizens at least a three tile width travel area, helps reduce collisions). Landscaping and terraforming are wonderful additions to the city building experience.
Sure, this idea isn't new, it's been around long before "the other game" was ever a thought. The excitement comes from new visuals, better graphics, unique implementation, and a more harsh challenges that will creep up on you right about the time you think you have enough food, or enough warm clothes, or enough houses, or....
You get the idea. This game will push you. You have to plan, you have to think ahead, you have to GO SLOW. Kinda like real life, eh?
Now the bad part. Why...  why oh why, would you guys at Mindillusion stoop so low as to pick on a one man dev team from "another game" - a game that inspired you to make this one? Bad form. And the one reason I regret giving you my $25.
Pathfinding makes you feel like every one of your citizens was hit in the face with a rock at birth, unless you give them plenty of room. Building at night or in the winter is pretty impossible with the current combination of lighting scheme and highlight grids. You'll find yourself building way more barns than you should need, simply because you can't designate crop harvests, etc, to go to specific locations, as other games have done in the past. There IS a method for re-distributing food so you don't witness starvation on a mass scale while you sit on 35,000 units of food (I have literally witnessed this...  a couple times), but it doesn't come until "late game", once expeditions are readily completed. If the mule lives long enough. And you don't mind the fact that it only moves about 50 units of any given item per season or so.
There is talk of viking raids being added?  The absence of expressly required conflict is part of the charm of this game, so I hope that it's a seperate game mode or option, if and when it's implemented. Assuming they aren't busy trying to prove LiF:FV's dad can beat up Banished's dad, or whatever.
Game, as is:  8.0 / 10
Mindillusion PR rating: 2.0 / 10

Nothings as fun as kicking back playing a 4 man coop experience where you fight rats in the warhammer universe. I will be reviewing Warhammer: End Times- vermintide in a pro/ con style and finishing things off with my own opinion.
Pro:
Team work is key to victory. This sounds obvious but in a few games you can seriously one man army through missions. Not here, this game takes the l4d approach and requires the player to work as a team to further their chances of living.
Each character feels unique. Each character is sporting their own melee and long range weapon. That can provide variety in gameplay since each character is pretty much a different experience.
The enemies are well designed and have some variety. For starters the basic rats have many different looks to them. Thats nice to see multiple different versions of the same enemy but they do not closely look like the specials. You can tell the differece between the "hunter", "Spitter", "Tank", "Smoker", armored, and the chaingun rat.
Con:
False difficulty mechanic. Well when you choose your difficulty the game doesnt really change which is fine to a degree but the maps are pretty much scripted when it comes to enemies showing up, mostly the specials like the tank. If you choose hard mode you dont start with a healing potion.
Job system. Well remember when i said the characters are unique? That is both good and bad. The bad part is that some characters are best to handle specific situations. Thats a very big flaw since what if you are the last and put in a situation that your not specifically designed for? Sure every character can fight and kill all enemies but some do it easier than others.
Leveling system. It is cool on paper and i know games like overwatch has a level system that doesnt nothing but drop loot boxes. Here... what is this game's excuese? It is a coop game with a level up system that does nothing but unlock loot that better the player's abilities. It sounds good but in the long term it is very useless and provides little to no benifits or usefulness. If the leveling game the player some stat boost like an rpg with 4player coop elements in the mix then that would be pretty cool.
Loot. EIther when the player levels up or complete a mission the game rewards the player with loot. Either a weapon with random rarity that messes with the stats of the player or provides material to be used for crafting or unlocking a weapon's ability. I dont see the point in being a random loot system in l4d like game. It feels odd and out of place.
Level design doesnt compliment the game. There are moments where the game has these pits like in the last level and on the very last part of the level a "tank" shows up and can easily one shot you off the floor to your death. Another level would be the moment where you need to get powder kegs on to the boat. The "tank" can do the same thing and puch you into the water to you death. Sure most of the game isnt bad but these moments can really make a player quit the game.
Conclusion:
In short this game is a l4d clone with a warhammer skin to it. What it lacks is the mechanics that made l4d a great game. For l4d there is coding that checks the situation of the player and fixes things to provide an experience that doesnt destroy flow. If the character is low on hp then the game eases up a bit. This game does not have that, it feels like it is completely scripted in a sense that the game doesnt provide any sense of maintaining flow. Things happen and you will die alot because of this. Also the lack of medical supplies make the game feel cheap when it comes to difficulty. The level up system provides no advantage or use besides giving the player a loot drop. I could easily continue on with game flaws but then i would be here all day and i just want to move on to better games. If you want to play 4 player coop experience i say go play l4d2 it is far better than this game could ever be or do payday 2, another nice game that can be an enjoyable experience with friends and randoms alike.

You will often see this game compared to left 4 dead, and while there are some striking similarities rat ogre = tank that can jump, gutter runner = teleporting hunter. That isnt always a bad thing. Left 4 Dead 2 is 8 years old and could do with a refresh.
Overall there are more levels though shorter each is probably around half to a third the length of a regular left 4 dead campaign but with no safe room checkpoints to space it out.
There are 5 different characters each with their own personality and weapon sets unlike L4D in which the only difference between the characters is their personalities and appearance.
Each character has 3 or 4 ranged and 3 or 4 melee weapons, you dont start with these you have to earn them through the loot system. Unlike Left 4 Dead this game is melee based so your main weapon is going to be some variety sharp pointy implement such as daggers, 1 handed sword, 2 handed sword, hatchet, battle axe,mace, or warhammer (no its not pointy or sharp but how could you have a warhammer styled fantasy game and not have a warhammer as a weapon).
specials are much more frequent often 2 or 3 at a time on higher difficulties and with more variety than seperate the players from each other. They are focused on killing you rather than seperating you so that the zombie hordes can finish you off.
Also different are some of the things that I found a little immersion breaking about left 4 dead such as approximately 500 zombies charging out of a bathroom stall or closet. Or the fact that AOE damage zombies like the spitter could land a HUGE pool of acid in front of you but other zombies could stand in it like it nothing more than a large puddle while it burned your team down in a matter of seconds. This is not the case in vermintide. Regular rats will climb out of rat tunnles or holes in the walls. The ratling gunner will pick a target and tunnel vision on them while firing hitting friend and foe and leaving him open to getting blind sided with a mace.
The globe lobber will throw poison gas grenades at your team which obscure vision deal out damage to people standing in it and also kill rats who run through it.
Additionally is an ability to ping targets of interest such as special rats or any kind of supply putting a glowing blue outline around it for your friends to see so no you longer have to do the look over here jumping/teabagging dance while over and over saying health over here, ammo over here, pills here!
Another difference is the characters, unlike left 4 dead where they are all in this together to survive many of the characters in vermintide enjoy making fun of each other or even outright hate each other. This comes out in the voice line interactions where the characters will make fun of each other for getting incapaciatated, attacked by various specials, or just for being low on health.
When this game first came out it had its share of bugs and slowdown during high action events. But now most of those isues have been fixed the processor that I was initially using and AMD 750k had a hard time running it but now it runs just fine.
Lastly one of my favorite things that fatshark did with their game is the pricing scheme for DLC
1. Some of the dlc is free: last stand and the bounty board.
2. The DLC that is paid is only $9 unless it goes on sale.
3. Did your friend just buy the DLC but you didnt? Guess what? If the game host has the DLC everyone else in their party can enjoy that same DLC content free of charge while in their party. and any loot that comes from the dlc is still usable after leaving the hosts game.
Overall I love this game just as much as I did the left 4 dead series and would highly reccomend it to anyone who liked left 4 dead but is maybe looking for something new to add to their list of co operative survival combat games to play with their rager friends who imideately press ALT + F4 as soon as they hit a challenge.

It's a fun game for the most part. Errors are punished severely and trying to Rambo by yourself will quickly lead to a defeat so cooperation, coordination and resource management are required. This make winning feel really satisfying. This is not without it's failings tho.
-Your melee, which is meant to be our primary source of dealing with things feels horrendously weak.
-There doesn't seem to be monster cossets and special units can literately spawn on you giving you no time to deal with them.
-How damage is calculated and distributed is head scratching at times. (Why allow a weapon to hit infinite amount of targets if its not going to do any damage to anything beyond the third target hit?).
-Tick damage (fire and poison) is laughable and nearly pointless.
-The bot AI is terrible (Take my advice, make sure some player plays the fire mage or she's gonna sit back and hold up your party blocking and pushing mooks rather the killing them)
-And speaking of pushing the storm vermin spam that stuff like it's going out of stye making them fairly infuriating to deal with when groups are about. (And unlike you have no apparent stamina and can just keep doing it endlessly.)
Tho the truly most boneheaded and foolish thing I've seen is the bounty board and how it can have DLC missions on it that are locked out from you to be able to take if you don't own it... yet you are allowed to go on the mission if one of your friends has the DLC, or even just joining a random pub. If you can do that, WHY LOCK THE DLC MISSIONS TO THE PLAYER?! It's asinine and giving the DLC is 10 bucks a piece when not on sale,(20 total) That's more then a little stupid if your going to let people invite there friends along on DLC mission. It's even more boneheaded when you realize the rewards FOR the mission (both the bounty board and DLC itself) aren't even DLC locked. So other then trying to be greedy to try and make people buy the DLC to get access to more key quest to unlock there bounty boar d missions, there is literately no point in doing this.
Would I recommend this game? Yes and no. But I'm going to mark it here as no. It is a fun 4 player game, honestly there's is no reason it could not be a 5 player game other then we have to keep it as L4D as possible for some reason. And I do enjoy when I play with my friends. But a lot of the problems mentioned above hurt the game enough that I could not recommend it. If those issues get attention and limiters are removed, I'll change my stance. I'll keep playing since I have it, but I can't recommend it to someone that doesn't.

I really don't understand the good reviews on this one. I am a huge fan of point and click/puzzle games. I love clever clues and connecting obscure bits of information to solve problems. While the premise (and trailer) set up what seems to be an intriguing plot and potentially interesting characters, don't expect any type of story or mystery here. You're the bad guy. You kill each person off and don't get a choice as to the order in which you do things, nor any freedom in HOW you remove each guest from the list. There is also no explanation for WHY these guests need to die, and when you are successful, it is uninteresting and ultimately unsatisfying.. Worst of all, you can only progress by clicking everything randomly and hoping something will happen, so there is no real reward for solving the "puzzles".
No atmosphere, no interaction with guests (they all stand around silently...), no heart, no charm. In short, no immersion.
I was very disappointed. Not worth the $2..

Basically this is a flash game. An actual, runs in Shockwave flash game like your papi used to play when he was goofing off  in computer lab in high school. That sets a lot of limitations for how sophisticated the game can be, but to it's credit there's a great aesthetic on display that works well with the format. In normal mode anyway. 'Effects on' mode is a big step down.
If you like amatuer games, room escapes and just plain batshit crazy stuff there's a lot to like here. But there's two GIGANTIC caveats here and if you can't get down with those, don't buy this game.
1) The moon logic on display here is absurd even by conventional moon logic standards. You got a guy to kill, and the game gives you a knife, but you're kidding yourself if you think you're just gonna insert Knife A into Victim B and call it a job well done. No, instead you have to use the knife SPECIFICALLY ON THE DUDE'S ANTLERS so you can get blood to make him a bloody mary because we're all about hospitality here at Rusty Lake. Then you poison the drink. Also I'm pretty sure a Bloody Mary doesn't have actual blood in it. And if it did who needs the poison at that point? Just kick back and let Hepatitis do it's dark work.
2) Because of the limitations of the format, there are a lot of places in this game where if you don't know exactly where to look for what, you will not be able to solve all the puzzles and achieve the best rank. If you know where everything is you can beat the game in about 30-40 minutes but if you're a perfectionist you're going to be spending a lot of time solving the same puzzles over and over again.

For the longest time I was looking for a game that would be something that would make me looking forward to playing it. One that had the charm of an older game with completely modern design and gameplay. One that had that unique feel to it that made you feel awesome playing it. One that had the detail throughout the entire game and one with difficulty that was constant throughout the entire game. One with unique characters, enemies, levels and story...
And this game was it, and boy am I glad that I bought it. It's funny because I had very little knowledge of this game before I bought it, and the only reason I bought it was because I caught a very short glimpse of it before switching pages on the Steam store. I thought, "Heck, why not try it?". I had bought games before and I had refunded them and I felt like I was being too picky and that I wouldn't find a game that I would have so much fun playing, but then I found this!
The game is great and there's a lot to cover, but I'll make a pretty short list of my favorite things from the game that made me love it.
The story was unique and unlike anything I have played before and the atmosphere of the game is just plain out weird. The enemies are pretty terrifying and the deaths are gruesome; there is no holding back in this game, there's no boundaries to gore in it. One of my favorite parts is in the very beginning where you're thrown in with the terrifying chainsaw butcher that you have to keep running away from: it's challenging, scary, and makes you want to kill that bloody ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Great opening to the game: a bloody butcher room with a crazy guy trying to cut you up.
But the game only gets better and you always feel on your toes. Ammo is always scarce and every pull of the trigger is a gamble. Enemies are difficult and the boss battles had me dying over and over again. Surprisingly, after playing through the whole thing, I only died 87 times!
This game resembles "The Last of Us" in several ways: custom death scenes, combat, collecting things, and story driven levels that always have something new to do in them. The detail on the levels in both games is gorgeous and I never found any glitch that made the level feel like it was cheap or like I was in a floating room. The only things that bothered me were clipping through walls at times and the reloading animations only had 1 animation: putting in two bullets regardless of your bullet count. Just like in TLOU, you can upgrade your character by collectibles and your upgrades are always very valuable, but you're never OP or feeling like the game could challenge you more. The game is very challenging and seems to always want to kill you every single turn you make, and it's plain awesome.
Last are the characters: Sebastian Castellanos, the main character, is a cool character and is in fact one of my favroite video game characters from gaming! The only thing I don't like about him is the fact he always seems so calm and collected and it sometimes kills the scare factor, simply because he himself doesn't seem worried about anything. His partners, Joseph and Kidmann are good characters as well, but there isn't too much to them. They appear quite often and they are likeable, but again not much too them. The main antagonist is creepy and has an interesting story behind him, always leaving you wanting to know more.
Finally, the story is great and you're always wondering what is going to happen next. Even after completing the game, I still have questions regarding some  of the things that occurred, but overall I understood it quite well. The concept is interesting and it's a unique idea. (at least from what I've played)
If you're thinking about buying this game, I HIGHLY recommend it! Goes down as one of my favorite games I have ever played, and hopefully I find another game that has the same effect on me as this one had on me.

There are games like America's Army: Proving Grounds, or Team Fortress, et cetera. Well, they both are at the pretty same level.
It's up to you. If you're very fond of this game, and if you have a change of 20$ in your pocket, then go for it. But if you're smart enough, and calculating your budget,  you might prefer to buy two games with better graphics and maybe even better concept, for the same price.

Binary Domain suprised me.
There's not a lot of games that managed to do that- after a rather boring and generic intro level (some 10 minutes of it) I was already starting to regret buying it, and ready to write it off as yet another generic cover based shooter.
Then came the intro. And I was sitting up in my chair, getting very interested in the drama all of a sudden. It was GOOD. The plot was intriguing, the characters actually had personalities, the voice acting was top notch, and they got actual Japanese voice actors to play Japanese characters, which is both a big bonus in my book, and makes the game feel anime-like a LOT.
The cutscenes are pretty much what makes this game good, like with Metal Gear Solid series. There's plenty of them, they have excellent direction and they have managed to get me hooked on the story, and even make me laugh out loud a few times!

I am enjoying this game way more than I expected to. As everyone has mentioned, this game draws heavily from Left 4 Dead. It feels like a totally different and unique experience though and that is what really makes it great in my opinion. The loot system is addictive and all the different game mechanics really set it apart from being just a L4D/zombie/horde killing clone. You get a real sense of accomplishment when you beat a mission after collecting all the tomes and grimoires within. I know nothing about the Warhammer universe but this game has enough personality to interest me in learning more. It is also worth mentioning the graphics; they are very nice and, as a result, quite demanding. I have almost all CPU/GPU-intensive settings turned to medium or lower to avoid big frame drops, yet the game still looks great. I also thought it was nice how each individual setting tells you how much CPU/GPU impact it has.
The only real complaint I have, as many others have mentioned, is the bot AI. Often times you will drop down a hole or off a ledge and eventually get dragged off/swarmed by enemies because the bots stop following you at the drop-off and just stand there, not even attacking with ranged weapons when they are just 5 feet above you. It is also very annoying when you turn around and see that they have left you alone and all backtracked half a mile just to kill one rat that spawned behind you. It is literally impossible to get past wave 4 on Last Stand with all bot teammates. Luckily though there are still plenty of people playing online and it is very easy to jump right into a match.
Overall it is a great game and somewhat refreshing after playing so many generic FPS/zombie games over the years. I would recommend to anyone interested,

If your going to clone a game. The right way to do it is to at least distinquish the gameplay an bring something new to the table. And that's what Vermintide does to the Left 4 Dead co-op formula. While co-op zombie killing games are common now. There actually really are not that many games that come close to L4D in quality. And most feel like a rehash of the same tired kill zombies concept. This game put's a medieval fantasy spin on the apocalypse by putting you into the Warhammer fantasy version of it during the End Times. Specifically in a Human city being invaded by the race of Rat Men the Skaven.
They are clever stand in's for Zombie's since they use the same kind of swarm tactics but have their specialist units too that can fill the roles most of the L4D mutant zombies did. However for all the similarities to L4D what makes the game worth playing if you already played L4D to death is the differences. Where as L4D focused on gunplay. Vermintide is a Melee focused game. If you played games like Chivalry you will have an idea of how it plays. It's a lot of more satisfying than L4D's pretty basic melee weapons. Which is needs to be since ammo is limited an you rely more on melee in Vermintide.
The game also seperates itself a bit from L4D by having a loot system. Because what is any fantasy era game without loot to collect, and equip to upgrade your chances of survival. I especially like how you can increase your chance of getting better loot by picking up items that are useless for any other purpose, and take up your Healing slots or even reduce your health. So your team if they are feeling confident can artifically boost the difficulty for better rewards. The one thing Vermintide lacks though is any kind of Versus mode. It's purely a co-op game. It might be a deal breaker for some so it's worth mentioning. But IMO this is one of the better co-op titles on steam right now, and definitely worth a play if you like the L4D style formula.

Fantastic game.  Very well designed with excellent, immersive graphics and sound.  The voice acting is top notch, and the characters are always bantering back and forth.  You'll want to take some time to explore every nook and cranny of the superbly detailed levels, but you won't have time.  Rats will swarm around you constantly, crawling out from every hole in the ground and crack in the walls and ceilings.  Hordes will stampede you and your friends as you run down dark corridors.
The combat is visceral and very satisfying, constant action.  You can decapitate, chop their arms and legs off, cleave them in twain with swords or crush their head like a mellon with brutal hammers.  Incinerate them with fireballs or put and arrow between their eyes.  The game rewards skill and takes a fair bit to succeed at.  Score a headshot and you can one shot some of the tougher rats.
Wander off from your friends and you're screwed.  A lone wolf doesn't last long in the savage warrens of Vermintide.  You'll have to learn the crucial skills of teamwork quickly if you want to succeed.
Once you get all that down, this is primarily a gear grinding game.  There are no stats on the characters, and while you can level up it doesn't grant you more health or anything other than a free item each time you level up.
Not that grinding for gear isn't fun, if you're the type who enjoys that.  Find a weapon that fits your playstyle and you can improve it, building it for the traits you prefer.

Gran juego con temática un tanto original, que recuerda a la peli "Yo, Robot". La jugabilidad es buena, a lo Gears of War pero con estilo propio; los gráficos son decentes, destacan las partículas de los robots al romperse y los modelados y variedad de los mismos. El argumento es de diez puntos, con buena carga emocional y giros argumentales, además que según la confianza que tengas con los personajes pueden ir cambiando las escenas y el final. Las últimas horas son totalmente épicas, al igual que los combates con los diferentes bosses. Hay humor, amor, traición, etc. Los personajes son muy carismáticos y además no faltan las típicas bizarradas japonesas. Podés responder a lo que te dicen de varias formas... y por micrófono, opción que a mí me funcionó bastante bien.
Como punto negativo diría que el MP está totalmente muerto, que la interfaz es mala, dejando en claro que es un port, y que la música tecno que tiene es medio repetitiva. Igualmente no deja de ser totalmente recomendable.

A Gears of War-type third person shooter with a crazy (but awesome) JRPG-style plot.  The gameplay is centered around cover-based shooting against hordes of robots and frequent boss battles.  Yes, it has regenerating health and some QTE sequences, along with a half-baked voice command feature that is best left disabled.  When the game was first released on PC it suffered from horrible controls, but this was corrected in later patches.  It's still an abvious console port, and you have to use a seperate utility launcher outside the game to change most options, but in the end, you can easily use either a kb/m or a gamepad.
The gunplay is awesome - the weapons feel powerful and the hit detection on the robots enemies is excellent.  You can destroy individual limbs and they react appropriately, changing weapons to another hand or crawling on the floor.  The boss battles are different enough to be engaging, but all come down to shooting the glowing spot enough times.  The game does set peice battles well.
However, the big draw here is the plot.  It's rare an FPS has an engaging storyline with even a decent script - this has both.  It's probably the most interesting and fun FPS I've played since Bulletstorm and it has a few plot twists that were actually unexpected.
Pick this up, especially if it's on sale.  I've seen it as low as $10 and it's a steal at that price.  You'll get 6-8 solid hours of fun out of it (but not much more unless you replay the campaign, multiplayer is dead.)

Okay, let's me be honest about this: I was one of the people that fought to get this game into Steam in the first place. I was hyped about this game for a long time because I'm a huge fan of STALKER and figured this game could scratch that itch.
And it did.
The issues comes from the continued scratching of said itch, which this game cannot accomplish. The initial joy of entering a STALKER-like world is quickly removed as you realize how unpolished the game is. Normally this COULD be forgivable but in the case of sZone Online that actually creates a serious issue: The game is so unpolished it feels unstable and makes playing the game a difficult chore. I watched as at times I was tearing through mutants and players alike while at other times I would be killed by a mutant that was stuck in the ground or constantly stuck in an anomally even after respawning OR you get missions that aren't translated from Russian and THEN find out the mission is broken in the first place, so there was never a point. For times like these you NEED older veteran players to give you a hand because they MIGHT have the items you need before bad coding removed said items, etc.
What killed it for me, however, was simply how dull it began to feel over time. The game doesn't really present any decent progression. When you get to the Camp (if you play you'll know where I'm talking about) there's really not major reason to keep going. At that point moving on feels more like a hinderence and a nuisance while staying only makes the whole experience stagnant. That word, right there, is what this game is: STAGNANT.
As a free game I would recommend it to scratch that STALKER itch, but really you're just going to have to wait for a better game to come along to give you some ointment for said itch.

Layers of Fear pulled me in from the very first moment of gameplay and didn't really let go until the final ending. It's visually beautiful, paintings, drawings, colorful ideas and all sorts of hidden things creep in the dark around you as you walk through a neverending house or - better said - a living nightmare. While for you it's going to be just a creepy house with a bunch of scares at first, it's actually a walk through the main character's twisted mind. The story itself is pretty simple but told in such an entertaining way that you're going to collect everything you can to get just a little bit more of it. And as a bonus, you can get one out of three different endings!
The only negative which I got to admit is that as the game heads towards the very ending, it's atmosphere is getting kind of weak although various creepy things are happening (maybe that's the reason- too many things happening). But that didn't ruin the game for me.
9/10. Don't look back.
