However, Layers of Fear successfully made me feel terrified from the beginning. I was genuinly afraid what lurked around the corners or even behind me. What I love about the "behind me" moments is that you aren't told to do so in the game (save for one time). Very pleasing graphics, eerie sounds, and a dark atmosphere pave the way for full horror immersion. Several times I had witnessed unsettling events and quickly turned around with a "NOPE", but was forced to gather up courage and progress. The manipulation of the rooms and the mind twisting events that happen really provoke you to not trust anything. The house itself becomes a character, trapping you in endless circles and corridors. A definite must-buy for any psychological horror fan.
By far THE best psychological horror game I have ever played! I would explain why, but I highly suggest you find out for yourself. I really hope they make a sequel or at least another one like this!

What can I say about this sad, deep game?  Let's start with the obvious.  It looks gorgeous to the eye of the beholder.  It starts out where you play as a man who is trying to solve the mystery of this house and you find a painting that is yet to be finished.  You have to proceed through the house where there are some paths that you branch off from and you find pieces of the mystery other than the pieces that are needed to finish the painting.  The atmosphere is absolutely stupendous.  When played on optimal settings, the darkness looks oppressively dark so much to the point that you don't want to proceed down this hallway that leads to the abyss...
There are some ways that you can die and yes, there is something out there that wants to get you.  As to who that is, you'll have to find out, but holy hell, I didn't want to meet it.
The sounds melds with the visuals to create a psychedelic horror experience that goes beyond things like Amnesia: The Dark Descent, Alien: Isolation, or especially Slender: The Arrival.
There is no sprinting in this game, but the reason why is explained when you continue playing the game.  Honestly, I didn't mind the loss of a sprint mechanic as the game still feels rich with atmosphere and absolute oppression that really makes you not want to progress.  When a horror game makes you NOT want to progress even though you KNOW you have to, then that means that it is doing its job.
Hell, the credits are cleverly put in for this game.
To Bloober Team SA, thank you so much for the experience, but I also hate you so much for creeping me the hell out.  Please, keep making more experiences that people will never forget...  For better or worse. Hahaha.
I give this game, Layers of Fear, a 90 out of 100 and I do highly recommend this game to any horror connoisseur out there.

[TL;DR AND "IS THIS GAME FOR ME?" AT BOTTOM]
is a game quite unlike any other. To add a bit of backstory, I purchased the game in Early Access back in October 2015 after being intrigued by the original idea and was instantly blown away by the amount of polish there was in an unreleased game. Even in its unfinished state,
had gorgeous graphics, a well-designed story and campaign, and even a fun event for Halloween (which i accidentally got stuck in.. but besides the point). As time went on, updates changed the game and added new rooms to gameplay, which made the game replayable with every update because there was always new stuff to find.
After being so thoroughly impressed with the Early Access version, I was ecstatic when the final product came out. I restarted the game from the beginning and found myself enjoying it just as much as I had the first time around. In
, you play as a painter who buries himself away in his house, going mad as he desperately tries to finish his final masterpiece. Without spoiling too much, the game has extremely sad undertones and tells a very tragic story, should you choose to listen. However, many players won't have the gut to scavenge for story items due to how terrifying and fast paced the game is. Although
can be described as a "walking simulator," it's definitely anything but dull and boring. Most of the game revolves around the mechanic of things changing behind your back while you're not looking. The entire experience is played out without a single loading screen, and this entire idea is pulled off extremely well. That being said, if you find it difficult to maneuver the world and control the camera angles in 3D games, this one may simply not be for you. Many of the scares require you to look at a certain place at a certain time, which is quite easy to do if you're used to video games, but if you aren't so good with 3D, the full effect of the game may be lost on you.
Now let's talk about the scares themselves -  you can't have a good horror game without it being scary, right? Now let me say just one thing: this game is absolutely terrifying. If it isn't the scariest game I've ever played, then it's still in my top 3, no questions asked. The gorgeous graphics and flawless sound design create a gripping atmosphere at all times, and there was never a moment in the entire campaign where I wasn't on the edge of my seat, waiting to see what was going to happen next. The best thing this game has going for it is that it's original. While games like
(2013) had you running away from horrific beasts in gruesome locations,
's horror is very different. Some may say that
is filled with cheap jumpscares, but it really isn't. While the jumps are frequent, it's really the psychedelic aspect that brought out the fear in me. It's extremely difficult to explain how the scares work in this game, but even the trailers don't do it justice. This game will have you spinning in circles and watching the entire room change with every rotation. It's no joke. The jumpscares, along with the psychedelic elements and the changing rooms behind every door, will have you trembling each time you open a door at night for weeks. Not to mention that the game generally moves at a brisk pace, with a kind of BOOM scare, move to next room, BOOM another scare, etc etc, which makes it all the more terrifying each time you run away from something right into something else. I wouldn't watch too many videos on this game before playing it to get a feel for what I'm saying though, because when you see all the scares a room has to offer before you enter it, they can be a little less exciting.
Unfortunately, there were a few moments in the game where doing something can become ever so slightly tedious or repetitive (
), which pulls you out of the moment. In a game that's very atmosphere-centric, this can be a problem, if not only a minor one. It's also worth mentioning that the game features quite a few cleverly designed puzzles that feel challenging, but never unfair. One thing I didn't like about the update to the final game was that it added female narrative along with the player's own thoughts, which made it seem less introspective and personal. The fact that there was only one actual character with a voice actor in the game made it feel quite lonely and added to the experience. Although this is only an opinion, I feel it was important to add for the sake of being thorough.
All in all, Layers Of Fear is a horror game I know I won't soon forget. With a completely original concept (something the horror genre overall has been lacking lately), unique scare tactics, clever puzzles and a fantastic atmosphere, Bloober Team has definitely hit the nail on the head with this one. The game is also highly replayable, as there are hundreds of cabinets to open and tons of things to find, as well as rooms that you can't visit by playing through the game only once.

Since Steam had the gall to recc me this game in the new Steam Discovery update, I thought I'd write a review of the game in it's current state since it's abandonment.
This game used to be GREAT. I bought Monday Night Combat a few months before Super MNC was released, and enjoyed a few hours of it but never got into it addictively. When Super MNC came out I was all over it. It was free2play, had a lot more options, characters, and got quite a bit of hype from a tie-in with Team Fortress 2 and one of the first games to incorporate Steam trading. It had a multitude of modes, a competitive but somewhat friendly community, and there were little to no problems besides a few occasional glitches to ruin the experience.
Then the devs/publishers threw the community under the bus. They insisted while they were working on Planetary Annihilation that they'd continue support for this game, even if it meant just minor updates/champ rotation/fixes. But they outright lied, and never officially announced abandoning the game and left the cash shop open. The matchmaking is completely broken, there's some BS number in-game that states how many players are on, and the community is just a few random vets with complete newbies who have no idea the game is dead, with a huge gap of experience/character upgrades between these two groups.
Uber is by no means a helpless small indie developer that doesn't have the resources to continue support for this game. Uber received over 2 million US dollars in Kickstarter money (with a project goal of 900k) for their new game, Planetary Annihilation, which has turned out into a slight disappointment in my opinion; although a few people in the Steam User Forums will insist the game's poor performance and their promise of offline -play is only because "they [Uber Entertainment] just needs more money/time". After receiving this large sum of money, Uber also charged $90 for alpha access to those who did not donate to their Kickstarter, and $50 for beta, all the while keeping silent on Super MNC and continuing to let it rot. This gives you an idea of Uber's recent shortcomings although you're free to look into them yourself and come to your own conclusions.
Another recent Super MNC reccomendation writer stated that Uber has stated on their forums they have interest in reviving this game if "given the chance", but they've had plenty and I hope these are not empty words. I'd love to continue to convert friends back to this game, even if Uber didn't do content updates but fixed matchmaking and updated Pro rotation.

I discovered this game thanks to Jessimew, and I loved it since the beginning. I played around version 0.1.5, and the game has improved in some ways since then -- but it also has gotten a LOT more complicated. I'm going to attempt to tackle each issue with thought and give credit where it is due. Thank you for taking the time to read this.
First thing's first, back in 0.1.5, for those who did not play back then, I'll simplify it for you. Back in the day, each action consumed your "berries" or "food source." It was extremely tedious work, and I'm very glad that the development team found a way around this -- so now your food source is diminished by how many pack members you have each day that passes. Not only is this more logical when it comes to how often food is consumed by animals in real life, it makes surviving a bit more enjoyable when it comes to collecting food.
However, the new user interface ( UI ) has gotten much more complex. Where you could once easily check your nichelings dominant and recessive genes, it has now become an entangled mess. While I get why they wanted to make it look more appealing with a DNA strand design, it is very confusing to the eye. I liked having one column for dominant genes, and yet another for recessive. For new players, some may be unable to identify what is even recessive, and what is dominant when it comes to their nichelings genetics.
As for the new genes, I am very excited and in-love with all of them. I think maybe there should be a help guide to explain a bit more in-depth about the genes, as it is difficult to look at a giant board of them. When chosing what genetics you'd like to have in place for breeding, it is very confusing to look at. They should atleast be divided into seperate locations such as -- mutations for ears, mutations for color, mutations for the body shape, etc. etc.
Evenstill, there are lots more that the game could improve on -- but those were the main topics. I really do love this game with its adorable design, unique play-style, and much more. I'm glad that they've tried to make genetics into a fun topic to enjoy and indulge in, but until some of these changes are made -- I, personally, am still going to struggle with liking the game as a whole.
Thanks yet again for reading! ~Shalefoot

A truely haunting experience.
*Plot
it was an amazing story line, Im on the 13th out of 14th chapter at the time of this review. It was spotless, I truely felt grabbed in by the story. I could slowly peice together the idea of what is going on without requiring too much quess work. It isn't the same as playing bloodborne where the story can be whatever you want it to be. This game had a very powerful writer and he really expressed everything onto Ruvick.
*Connection to characters
Connection to characters is very important when looking at games, if a general person can not feel conected to a game, they alot of the fun is removed. I felt like I could fit in both the protagonist and antagonists shoes at both times which was very surprsing. The antagonist has strong angers towards everyone from his very taggic childhood experience, while the protagonist is constantly feeling shock and fear by being thrown into a carnival of horror.
*Controls
Highlighted controls on the screen that stay throughout the entire game. It doesn't leave you entirely in the dark and helps you get around difficult areas. The game has a very detailed and well informed hub about what is currently happening to you. Alot of information comes from the vibrations that come out of a controller. You might want to use a controller for this game. Just a warning is that there will be alot of shooting and the game doesn't assit you with your aim at all. Unless your sniping and it does auto aim there even with a mouse.
* General Thoughts
While I hated how I couldn't kill certain enemies and how the game really does it's best to prevent stealth but heavily rewards stealth at the same time. I feel this game did a very impressive job when it came to athmosphere, I felt surrounded by the story.  It had some very guessable jumpscares, but that knowing comes from playing and watching alot of horror. If you are on the edge about buying this game go watch a person play the firsrt chapter of the game. The first chapter gets you a feel of what your are expecting while not realising anything but who the main characters of the story are.
*Graphics
This game came out in 2014 which is two years ago from the writingf of this review. I would have to say the awkward aspect ratio and forced fps lock is annoying. The lock can be removed manually but when it comes to the aspect ratio you would have toi use a memory hack to fix that. That is increadbly annoying and quite hard to do considering memory hacks don't always work.
Because it was a console port it has some amazing artwork, most consoles can't render in more polygons or have multiple running effects at one time. So having a game have better made art makes the game seem beutiful, and allows for the GPU to relax. I am not saying any computer can run this game. I was running it on a 980ti at 1080p, I ran it perfectly but at a certain chapter I kept dropping to 8 fps and so on. It was annoying I gave my computer a restart and everything seemed to be alright. This sortof leads to my next point.
* Bugs and Glitches.
SO MANY BUGS! Honestly this was annoying. How many times I had the game crash, how many times I couldn't start the game up properly. This is all without the memory hacks. The memory hacks only made it worse, that is why I finally gave up to play on 1080p. This game is a mess and a terrible port, so many glitches when it comes to using a mouse, so many problems occur when trying to run this game. If you don't want your time wasted by restarting the game every hour then maybe this isn't the game for you.
*My recomendation
I will be giving this game a positive review, looking at the game from a perfectly non-bias review the game was enjoyable along with a pleasure to look at. Yes it did have many bugs, the controls are awkward and the game is realy hard.  If I had to truely give an opion I feel this game does do better then the average game you can find. If you have the stomach to amount past all that gore and are into this genre this game will do you good. If you can't deal with the horric amount of bugs or don't want to play with a controller then this game isn't for you.

I am going to assume by the time you read this you have checked out some trailers of the game and you pretty much know what this game is about. In a nutshell the game is an intergalatic air hockey simulator in which you pick a Runner and try to score goals. You play against another team of up to 3 players. Matches last 5 minutes and if undecided run into sudden death, where a golden goal principe is enforced. I like the competive element of the game, it feels like a real sport.
First the bad: I tried the game a few months back and it was still very much an early access product. It lacked proper dedicated servers and the interface was cluncky at best. It also had quite a few serious bugs, like loading screens timing out or games starting and not being balanced properly (3v2 or 1v4). At the time I quit, but hey, the game was in early access and it didn't claim to be anything else.
Now the good: About two weeks back I logged back in and was pleasantly suprised: dedicated servers, loading bugs completely fixed and a new slick interface (that naturally could still use some work here and there). It has come to a point where I would definitely recommend the game. There are still some issues, for example some problems with quests registering multiple times, but the core game itself is solid, fun and very easy to get into. The worst problem at the moment though is the limited number of players. Personally I don't mind playing some bots every now and again, but when this happens a lot the game loses some of its tension, because it is great to face off against other players. Besides, the game is free, so why not give it a bash.
My final thoughts? With some more players this game would be great fun. It feels amazing to score that deciding goal a few seconds before the timer runs out, let alone win a match that has run into sudden death by a well timed shot or a great long pass. Do yourself a favor and check out Arena: Cyber Evolution, or ACE for short.

This is an excellent horror game that's genuinely creepy and atmospheric. The music/sound is superb and the story is solid. This isn't a traditional horror game though, although you can "die" it really isn't a major setback, for example you won't have to do any puzzles over again if you die. Like Amnesia and related games there's no combat, you can flip levers, pull ropes and open up chests and doors though. Unlike Amnesia and most other horror games you don't have a portable lightsource, while this is mildly frustrating at times, its not as bad as it might sound though as the environments in Layers of Fear generally have atmospheric, but adequite lighting, candles, light bulbs and lamps abound. If you're a fan of Amnesia and related horror games, Layers of Fear is a must buy.
There are though some downsides:
* The game is fairly short at about 2 hours a playthrough. That said, there are multiple endings so there's some replay value there, but since the game takes the form of more or less a novel brought to life, this is unlikely to be a game to log hundreds of hours on.
* The game tended to lag at times, although it was never unplayable occasionally there was noticable slowness, likely due to Unity
* The game isn't all that difficult, you won't need a walkthrough for this one (unless you're going for achievements). While this isn't always a bad thing, it does leave the impression that your choices in the game don't really matter
* There are portions of the game that are repetitive, most rooms follow the same format which leads to you expecting a lot of the scares
Overall though this game is a must play if you're a fan of the horror genre. If you liked Amnesia, you'll love Layers of Fear. At $20 though its hard to recommend for casusal fans due to the short length of the game. However, if this game is on sale and you have any love for horror games at all, pick this one up.
Fans of Amnesia, etc. - 8/10
Everyone else - 6/10, jumping to a 8/10 if you can get this game on sale ($5-10 would be a good price for this game)

The game tries to be scary. It tries really, really hard. So hard that it ends up not scary at all. While the visuals are stunning, the game itself is not so much a horror game as a museum of horror game tropes. Remember that creepy thing you saw in that game? It's here. You walk from one room to another, wondering what kind of a jump-scare or a mind-screw they'll throw at you this time. Will it be a sudden bloody knife? A woman's shout? A wheelchair following you? A door you open to see a gigantic face staring at you?
The problem is, all these special effects are there on their own, existing for their own sake. In Silent Hill, Clocktower, Fatal Frame they served a purpose. Here the excuse plot is so formulaic I can't care about the story or the people. So, while you might enjoy the attractions, there's nothing else to it -- lots of hard work and artistic talent put into creation of a catalogue of cliches.

Do I think this game is fun?
Yes, I do
But, would you?
This game is long and drawn out, at least in my opinion. It's slow paced sometimes and may be tedious, but its a good game.
The goal is to survive in an unforgiving wilderness, with only your wits and whatever Nichelings you find, but how?
In Niche, you can mold and bend your little creature's genetic material to an extent, though it doesn't give you complete freedom. Each Nicheling is different in one way or another, whether its physical capability or appearance.
Breeding combines the genetics of the parents, sometimes you may just end up with a clone of a parent.
Over a hundreds of different combinations allows for breeding to be a wildcard. With certain match ups, you could breed complete trash, or a force to reckon with.
You also have to worry about feeding this niche of creatures. Each consumes 1 food per day, which is not as bad as back in the earlier versions. Foods sources you can use are berry bushes, trees (nuts,) fish, AI critters that can stumble upon your pack, and more!
With careful managing, your niche can thrive. Just watch out for those Rogue Males, who'll seek any females of your pack and mate with them. As you progress, you may start getting bored of your island, or you've cleared it off. When you do, you can send 7-8 Nichelings to the next island, who knows where you'll end up. Theres the forbidding jungle, where apes of different senses can wipe out the weakest of the pack. Large, predatory carnivores that are more of a nuisance than a real predator sometimes. Then theres the mountains, an unwelcoming place with dangerous creatures, and not much food to go with it too.
Niche is visually appealing, with nice graphics to go along with the great gameplay. The music is lovely too, and I have no complaints here.
Overral, Niche can be difficult, or easy, depending on how you'd like to play it. Its aesthetically pleasing and very fun if you have the patience. If you don't like games were you play god, I wouldn't suggest this.

Sniper Elite: nazi Zombie Army 2 is the first full game of Sniper Elite that i played (i played SE v2 demo but it was few years ago :P) and i must say that i love this game. Now sometimes the game can make you rage, swear and curse creators of the game, but after few tries you realise what did you do wrong, and you fix your mistake, and then progress with a "banana" on your face.
Gameplay :
This version is kinda varied from other Sniper Elite games. Mainly because you wont use your sniper rifle that often. Another diffrence, is that you actually shoot zombies, that melee you, instead of shooting enemies. Well, there are Zombie Snipers, that kinda sounds stupid and unrealistic, but i'll explain that later. I really like the balance between needing to use your sniper, and full options to use any weapon you want.
Story (NO SPOILERS) :
We start with a cutscene of Hitler speaking to one of his generals (i couldnt identify him closely, but that doesnt really matter) about the Relics that supposed to keep the zombies in control. We get to know that Nazis had some Relics that let them control these zombies. Our mission is to get in the possesion of those, and stop the Nazi Zombies. As simple as it gets, i dont play the game too much for the story. The story isnt anything super great, but i dont mind it.
Realism :
Now I could even dig it that Nazis got some super zombie virus that let them to take over the whole Europe or something, but they got some magical relics, that control zombies. What is that ? I mean i dont hate it, but you could atleast implement some more realism in that part. The only thing that i understand about that, because it actually matches the story, is the Zombie Snipers i mentioned before. I mean, they can somehow fly, but i guess creators though of him being somehow powered by magic of the relics or something like that. They are kinda annoying because, you scope in, and they jump to another position, but i guess it is supposed to be the diffrence from other games.
Difficulty :
I am playing this game on the hardest difficulty, and i must say that it isn't that hard as i expected but in some parts It can get frustrating. I guess i could finish the game on easiest in about 4-5 hours. As i read some other people's reviews, they finished on hardest in about 9-10 hours, I didnt finish the story yet (writing this at Friday, the 13th) but i guess im gonna have a time around that, maybe even faster.
Pros :
+Balanced difficulty
+A good variancy from other Sniper Elite games
+Good gameplay
+Nice Graphics
+Sound effects are good
+Bullet cams are cool as always
Cons :
-Not that realistic as expected
-Zombie Snipers are more annoying than challenging
-No local cooperation mode
Overall : 7.5/10

After playing Ace of Spades for over a day's worth of time, you know what it's like.
_The gameplay. That's what keeps this game going. All the gamemodes; Team deathmatch, Capture the Flag (Classic and Standard), VIP, Zombie, and more. You can build your own structures while in-game, and you can make your own maps. Plenty of Steam Workshop maps.
_The graphics are... meh. Standard voxel graphics? I guess. Super simple, plain blocks. Not a strong point in this game.
_AoS has some interesting zombie sounds 'n' stuff. Cool soundtrack. Solid audio.
_The community? Eh, it's okay. Plenty of players if you wanna play CTF or Zombie, but other than those two gamemodes, not a whole lot of activity. You never know if you are gonna run into a friendly server or not.
_Now, for my personal opinion: You can play this game as much, and for however long you want. I would buy this game for full price again for sure, but look out for sales, I seen it for $3.75 before. I have had, and will continue to have, a blast with this game. Ace of Spades won't go down in history as one of the best games ever (it has it's haters), but I certainly have enjoyed it.
